audits.name: Boost decomposition of (U, Gamma) as standard Misner-Sharp-Hernandez kinematics

source.located: W. C. Hernandez & C. W. Misner, ApJ 143, 452 (1966), and C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964). Neither is on arXiv. The MSH formalism was read through arXiv restatements: Helou, Musco & Miller arXiv:1601.05109v6 (CQG 34, 135012, 2017) pp.3-6, 8-11, 30. Their p.3 footnote says MSH is 'a composite' of MS 1964, HM 1966 and May & White 1966. Also read: Faraoni, Ellis, Firouzjaee, Helou & Musco arXiv:1610.05822 (PRD 95, 024008) pp.5-8, 12-13; Escriva arXiv:2504.05813v3 (2025) pp.3-5, 12. The invariance was cross-read in Hayward arXiv:gr-qc/9408002v2 pp.3-4, 16.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1601.05109, 1610.05822, 2504.05813, gr-qc/9408002 and 2601.03077. HM 1966 and MS 1964 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ. The explicit two-observer boost U' = cosh w U + sinh w Gamma, Gamma' = sinh w U + cosh w Gamma was not found printed as-is in any source read. What the restatements do print: (i) U = D_t R and Gamma = D_r R, both in the fluid's comoving frame; (ii) Gamma^2 - U^2 = gradR.gradR = 1 - 2M/R; (iii) HMM eq.(15), dR/dtau = U + Gamma v; (iv) Faraoni eqs.(4.16)-(4.17), the comoving-vs-Kodama gamma_rel = (1 - U^2/Gamma^2)^-1/2 with |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|. The boost follows from (iii) plus time dilation (check C1).

audits.published_statement: Helou-Musco-Miller 1601.05109 p.5, eqs.(3)-(6): 'In the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez approach, two basic differential operators are introduced D_t = (1/a) d/dt and D_r = (1/b) d/dr, representing derivatives with respect to proper time and radial proper distance in the comoving frame of the fluid ... U = D_t R ... Gamma = D_r R ... related to the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass M ... by the constraint equation Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R'. Eq.(9): 'M = (R/2)(1 - grad_a R grad^a R) with grad_a R grad^a R = Gamma^2 - U^2'. Eq.(15)-(16): '(1/a) dR/dt = dR/dtau = (U + Gamma v), where v = (b/a) dr/dt is the 3-velocity of the object ... measured with respect to the local comoving frame of the fluid.' Faraoni et al 1610.05822 p.5: 'all spherically symmetric foliations will produce the same apparent horizons (but this is not true of non-spherical foliations)'. Faraoni eqs.(4.16)-(4.17): 'u^a_(K) u_(C)a = -1/sqrt(1 - U^2/Gamma^2) = -gamma(v_rel) ... |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|'. Hayward gr-qc/9408002 p.4: 'Note that E is an invariant.'
published_hypotheses: spherical symmetry of the spacetime (HMM p.4; Hayward p.2)
MSH setting: diagonal comoving 'cosmic time' metric -a^2dt^2 + b^2dr^2 + R^2dOmega^2, with u^a = (1/a,0,0,0), i.e. the fluid's comoving foliation (HMM eq.2; Escriva eq.2.2)
perfect fluid (HMM eq.7). It is needed for the MSH evolution equations and for M as a volume integral of e, but NOT for the kinematic identity Gamma^2 - U^2 = gradR.gradR
HMM p.5: 'a, b and R are positive definite'. The sign of Gamma is not fixed there, and Escriva p.12 reports Gamma < 0 occurring in type-II data
units c = G = 1
gradR.gradR is foliation-independent only across spherically symmetric foliations (Faraoni p.5)
in HMM eq.(15), tau is the COMOVING proper time
hypothesis_drift: BROADENED, and the broadening is supported. MSH defines U and Gamma in the fluid's comoving frame for a perfect fluid (HMM p.5). foliation.py:108-116,128-134 applies them to any spherically symmetric unit timelike u, with no matter model. This is supported because the boost and the invariant are identities of the metric alone: re-derived here for free Phi, Lambda, R, w (A1-A9) and for a 2-metric with shift (B1-B4).
KEPT: restriction to spherically symmetric foliations. It is stated at foliation.py:110 but not repeated at :145-148 or in GAMMA_RANGE / INVARIANT_CRITERION (foliation.py:856, 858).

DROPPED IN PROSE, KEPT IN z3 (a tree-side drift that affects downstream corollaries, not the boost). The orientation Gamma > 0 is absent from the range and the biconditional at foliation.py:140-148, 856, 858. The z3 obligations do carry G > 0 (foliation.py:790, 809, 812, 843-844), and the prose names it once at :156. Reverse n and Gamma lies in (-inf, -k]; then 'Gamma > 1 in every foliation' fails at m < 0 (F2, computed), while |Gamma| > 1 still holds (F3). No orthochronous boost can flip the sign of Gamma (E6, z3 unsat).
KEPT: orthochronous boosts only, with c > 0 (foliation.py:798-799).

DISCREPANCY, misprint-class, recorded and not repaired: foliation.py:129 writes 'U = -u^a d_a R', but the code at foliation.py:635 and :649 uses U = +u^a d_aR, which is also the MSH sign (HMM eq.4). Under the docstring's sign the boost at :132 holds only with w -> -w (G2). The invariant is unaffected (G1).

ATTRIBUTION NARROWER THAN WORDED: foliation.py:381-382 calls this 'standard Misner-Sharp-Hernandez kinematics'. The ingredients are MSH and were read. The cosh/sinh boost formula itself is special-relativistic kinematics of the covector dR, obtained from HMM eq.(15) plus time dilation, and is not printed in any source read. driven.py:70-71 already records HM 1966 as NOT CONSULTED.

rederivation.outcome: 31 checks, none with an unwanted outcome (exit 0). A1-A9: U = e^{-Phi}R_t, Gamma = e^{-Lam}R_r, gradR^2 = Gamma^2 - U^2; with a free w(t,r) the boosted frame is orthonormal and U', Gamma' and the invariant come out exactly as foliation.py:132-134 prints them. B1-B4: the invariant also holds in an ADM 2-metric with shift. C1-C2: HMM eq.(15) plus time dilation, with v = tanh w, gives the boost. D1-D3: the tree's psi equals Faraoni's comoving-Kodama gamma_rel and |v_rel|. E1-E3: the tree's O12 witness is c = cosh(psi2-psi1), s = sinh(psi2-psi1). z3: transitivity proved on the Gamma>0 branch (E4, unsat, with vacuity guard E5), and no orthochronous boost crosses branches (E6, unsat). F2 is a computed counterexample to the prose form that omits orientation: m=-1, R=10, n inward gives Gamma < 1 on every foliation; F3 shows |Gamma| > 1 still holds. G1-G2 cover the docstring sign; H1 shows the trapped branch covers all real Gamma.

later_literature.what: Restates the MSH composite: U, Gamma, Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R, M = (R/2)(1 - gradR^2), and eq.(15) dR/dtau = U + Gamma v, from which the boost follows.

later_literature.ref: Faraoni, Ellis, Firouzjaee, Helou & Musco arXiv:1610.05822 (2017)
later_literature.what: The invariant is foliation-independent across spherically symmetric foliations but not across non-spherical ones (p.5). Gives the comoving-Kodama gamma_rel and |v_rel| = |U/Gamma| (eqs.4.16-4.17), which is the tree's psi measured from the U=0 slice.

Confirms the U and Gamma definitions and the constraint (eqs.2.3, 2.5). Also shows Gamma < 0 occurring in type-II data (pp.5, 12), the orientation case the tree's prose range leaves unnamed. This narrows the tree's downstream prose, not the boost.
E is an invariant, and the split into a spatial and a temporal direction is not unique (p.3). So the frame components of dr change with the frame while their norm does not.

Frame changes between foliation-adapted frames on the normal plane (sec.4.1, eqs.64-71), including non-spacelike slices. The orthonormal boost is a special case. This paper came from the discover_papers call, which found nothing contradicting the result.

audits.lacked_data: No measured datum enters. U, Gamma and the constraint are definitions plus algebra on a spherically symmetric metric, and the boost is special-relativistic kinematics of dR. Evidence that later data cannot move it: it holds for arbitrary Phi, Lambda, R and an arbitrary rapidity field w(t,r) (A1-A9), in a gauge with shift (B1-B4), and over 2000 random numeric states (N1). No field equation, equation of state or physical constant is used. What the authors had was a narrower scope, not missing data: they worked in the comoving frame of a perfect fluid, and the tree broadens that to any spherically symmetric observer, a broadening the re-derivation supports. The only framing problems found are in the tree: the Gamma > 0 orientation omitted from the prose (F2) and the docstring sign at foliation.py:129. Neither is a defect of the external result, and neither comes from missing data.
audits.grade_evidence: The boost as foliation.py:132-134 prints it was re-derived exactly in sympy, both for free w(t,r) with free metric functions and in a gauge with shift (31/31 checks). z3 proves the transitivity the tree relies on (E4). The MSH ingredients were READ via restatement (HMM eqs.4-6, 9, 15; Faraoni p.5 and eqs.4.16-4.17; Escriva eqs.2.3, 2.5), and the boost follows from HMM eq.(15) plus time dilation (C1). The broadening to any spherically symmetric observer is supported, and no datum is involved. Three findings are recorded, not repaired, and none changes the grade: (a) the cosh/sinh formula is not printed in any MSH source read, so 'standard MSH' is accurate for the ingredients only; (b) the prose at foliation.py:140-148, 856 and 858 drops the Gamma > 0 orientation that its z3 carries (F2 counterexample; |Gamma| survives); (c) the docstring sign at :129 disagrees with the code at :635/:649. HM 1966 and MS 1964 remain NAMED-NOT-READ.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: It would move to NARROWED if a downstream use (ledger D2, specthm fact D2 / class K0 / requirement R1) applies 'Gamma > 1 in every foliation <=> m < 0' where n points inward or Gamma < 0, for example across a wormhole throat with a single radial coordinate running mouth to mouth. It would also move to NARROWED if any use involves non-spherically-symmetric foliations, where Faraoni p.5 shows the invariance fails. Reading HM 1966 at source could firm up the attribution. No computation here points toward WRONG.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction): hernandez-misner-kinematics-boost-decomposition, graded STANDS
verifiers.reason:
I tried to break the STANDS grade in both directions and could not. The grade holds as the auditor gave it.

1. Sources re-read through alphaXiv:
- Helou, Musco & Miller arXiv:1601.05109v6. p.3 has the footnote calling MSH a composite of MS 1964, HM 1966 and May & White. p.5 has eqs.(2)-(9), with U = D_tR, Gamma = D_rR, Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R and gradR.gradR = Gamma^2 - U^2. p.8 has eqs.(15)-(16), dR/dtau = U + Gamma v, with v measured in the comoving frame.
- Faraoni et al. arXiv:1610.05822. p.5 says spherically symmetric foliations agree and non-spherical ones do not. p.13 has eqs.(4.16)-(4.17), gamma(v_rel) = (1 - U^2/Gamma^2)^-1/2 and |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|.
- Hayward gr-qc/9408002. p.4 says 'Note that E is an invariant'. p.12 has eq.(27), 1 - 2E/r = e^-mu r'^2 - rdot^2, the form Misner & Sharp actually gave. This is the eq.(27) that foliation.py:383 cites, and it is correct.
Every quotation in the audit matches the page text.

2. Machine checks:
- The auditor's script ran: 31/31 checks, exit 0.
- My own sympy check also passed, 7/7, exit 0. With free Phi, Lambda and R it gives U' = cosh w U + sinh w Gamma, Gamma' = sinh w U + cosh w Gamma, and the invariant unchanged.
- The docstring sign U = -u.dR at foliation.py:129 needs w -> -w for the boost as printed. That is misprint-class, as the audit says, and the code at :635 uses +u.dR.
- Hayward's eq.(27) reduces to Gamma^2 - U^2.
No datum enters the result, and the broadening to any spherically symmetric observer is an identity of the metric alone.

3. Downstream uses, checked against the audit's own conditions for moving to NARROWED:
- ledger.py:372-377, specthm R2 at :841-866, specthm K0 at :1551-1561 and H_R1 at :2201 all sit under H_sph. The axial throat is priced through O4/H_axial, not through D2. No use applies D2 across non-spherical foliations or across a wormhole throat with an inward-pointing n.
- A throat can never carry m < 0: at the throat Gamma = 0 on the static slice, so 1 - 2m/R <= 0 there and m >= R/2 > 0.
- Hayward p.3 defines 'outgoing' canonically on untrapped spheres (z(dr) > 0). So Gamma > 0 is the standard orientation and not an arbitrary one.
The orientation finding (b) therefore stays a prose omission on the tree side. ledger D2's 'nothing in 4D spherical symmetry' leaves that convention unnamed, but this is a downstream wording matter. It does not narrow the external result.

4. One correction to the audit, and it does not move the grade. Finding (a) says the cosh/sinh boost is 'not printed in any source read', and that is accurate. But it understates the support for 'standard MSH kinematics'. HMM p.5 calls Gamma 'a generalized Lorentz factor (which reduces to the standard one in the special relativistic limit)' and U 'the radial component of four-velocity in an Eulerian frame where R is used as the radial coordinate'. At k = 1 that is exactly Gamma = cosh psi and U = sinh psi = gamma v, which my check confirms numerically. So the boost reading is MSH's own interpretation, and only the explicit two-observer formula is missing from what was read.

HM 1966 and MS 1964 remain NAMED-NOT-READ. Nothing points toward NARROWED, WRONG, DATA-DEPENDENT or OPEN. verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION
verifiers.reason:
I copied the audit script to verify/rederive/hmk.py and ran it. It printed "31 checks, 0 with unwanted outcome" and exited 0, matching the audit's claim.

Is the encoding the theorem or a toy of it? It is the theorem as the tree uses it. A1-A9 work on the general spherically symmetric diagonal metric, with free Phi(t,r), Lambda(t,r) and R(t,r) and a free rapidity field w(t,r). B1-B4 check the invariant (not the boost) in an ADM 2-metric with shift; I confirmed that the normal (1/A, -s/A) is correct for ds^2 = -A^2dt^2 + B^2(dr + s dt)^2.

Caveats on the encoding, none of which changes the grade:
(1) A7 and A8 hold by linearity of the contraction. My guard NH shows the same form holds for arbitrary coefficients (a, b). So the real content of A1-A9 is A4-A6 (the boosted frame is orthonormal) together with A9 (the invariant).
(2) G2 checks only the U component of the w -> -w statement. The Gamma component also holds, which I checked by hand.
(3) F1-F3 sample psi in [-5, 5] rather than quantifying over all psi. The F2 counterexample needs no sampling, because -k cosh(psi) < 0 for every psi.
(4) The Frobenius / foliation-existence lemma (foliation.py V5) is not re-checked. The audit does not claim it for this key.

Vacuity guards (hmk_vacuity.py, 11 guards, 0 bad). I negated each hypothesis and every check fails as it should:
- Euclidean rotation in place of the boost: invariant fails.
- Non-unit boost with a free scale lam: fails, and holds again at lam = 1.
- Spherical symmetry dropped, either R(t,r,theta) or a t-theta cross term: gradR^2 differs from Gamma^2 - U^2. This matches Faraoni p.5.
- E4 without G2 > 0: z3 returns sat, so the counterexample exists.
- E4 at k = 0: sat.
- E6 without c > 0: sat, so the sign of Gamma can flip.
- N1 with a boost off unity by 0.1%: caught by the 1e-9 tolerance.
- A half-boost where n is not co-boosted: fails.
So no check passes with its hypothesis removed.

Additional finite check (hmk_exhaust.py, z3). Given u' = a u + b n with a^2 - b^2 = 1 and a > 0, the unit radial n' orthogonal to u' with q > 0 is forced to be b u + a n: negation unsat, with the vacuity guard sat. So orthochronous boosts exhaust the oriented orthonormal (t,r) frames. With the orientation q > 0 dropped, z3 returns sat. That independently backs the audit's finding (b), that the prose range and the biconditional need Gamma > 0.

Tree-side checks:
- foliation.py:129 reads 'U = -u^a d_a R'; :649 reads 'U = u^a d_aR'. The sign discrepancy is confirmed, and it is misprint-class.
- :381-382 does say 'standard Misner-Sharp-Hernandez kinematics'.
- :790 ident and :843 O12 carry G > 0, while GAMMA_RANGE and INVARIANT_CRITERION (:856, :858) do not.
- The in-file V4 uses positive=True on s, but it substitutes c^2 = 1 + s^2 in a polynomial identity, so the sign restriction is harmless.

No datum enters this result. The re-derivation supports the identity as the tree uses it, under its named hypotheses: spherical symmetry, an orthonormal frame, orthochronous boosts, and Gamma > 0 for branch statements. STANDS is the grade the evidence supports. The three recorded findings are tree-side or attribution matters, and none refutes the external result. HM 1966 and MS 1964 remain NAMED-NOT-READ.

audits.name: Painleve-Gullstrand / Lemaitre slicing of Schwarzschild: sqrt(2m/R) is the marginally bound free-fall velocity (Newtonian escape velocity)

source.located: Painleve, C.R. Acad. Sci. Paris 173, 677 (1921); Gullstrand, Arkiv Mat. Astron. Fys. 16(8), 1-15 (1922); Lemaitre, Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles A53, 51 (1933). All three are NAMED-NOT-READ (no arXiv copy). Read through exact restatements: Martel & Poisson arXiv:gr-qc/0001069 eqs (2.1)-(2.7), (3.1)-(3.6), (4.1)-(4.5) and Sec. V; Hamilton & Lisle arXiv:gr-qc/0411060 eqs (1)-(7); the Lemaitre chart as restated in de Haro arXiv:2601.18660 eqs (18)-(29); Faraoni & Vachon arXiv:2006.10827 eqs (1.3)-(1.14) and (4.1)-(4.9).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text: gr-qc/0001069 pp.1-6, gr-qc/0411060 pp.1-6, 13, 15, 2601.18660 pp.1-10, 2006.10827 pp.1-17

audits.published_statement: Martel-Poisson Sec. II. Radial timelike geodesics of Schwarzschild obey tdot = E~/f and rdot^2 + f = E~^2 (2.1), with E~ = 1/sqrt(1 - v_inf^2) (2.2). Specialising to E~ = 1 ('starting at infinity with a zero initial velocity') gives rdot = -sqrt(1-f) = -sqrt(2M/r). Then u_a = -d_a T with T = t + int sqrt(1-f)/f dr (2.3)-(2.5), and the metric becomes ds^2 = -dT^2 + (dr + sqrt(2M/r) dT)^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (2.7). In their words, 'the surfaces T = constant are intrinsically flat'. Hamilton-Lisle eqs (1)-(2): 'beta is the Newtonian escape velocity ... beta = (2GM/r)^(1/2) and t_ff is the proper time experienced by an object that free falls radially inward from zero velocity at infinity'; also 'inside the horizon, the infall velocity exceeds the speed of light'. Lemaitre chart (de Haro eqs 18, 28-29): trajectories with rdot = -sqrt(2MG/r) satisfy R - T = (2/3) r^{3/2}/sqrt(2MG), and ds^2 = dT^2 - (2MG/r) dR^2. The time coordinate is the same free-fall proper time as PG time.
published_hypotheses: Schwarzschild vacuum, M > 0. Faraoni-Vachon: PG observers do not exist where the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass is negative (negative-mass Schwarzschild, AdS, RN inside r = Q^2/2M)
radial, timelike, freely falling (geodesic) observers (MP Sec. II)
E~ = 1: starting from rest at infinity, i.e. marginally bound (MP eq 2.2, p = 1)
ingoing branch, rdot < 0: covers the exterior and the black-hole region but not the white-hole region; the time reverse gives the outgoing chart (MP Sec. II, Fig. 1)
the congruence is hypersurface orthogonal, which is automatic for radial motion; mu is constant iff the motion is also geodesic (MP Sec. V)
static generalisation (MP Sec. IV): the slices are flat only if psi = 0 and p = 1. Hamilton-Lisle: beta = sqrt(2M(r)/r), with Misner-Sharp M(r), for g_tt g_rr = -1

dynamic generalisation (Nielsen-Visser, restated in Faraoni-Vachon eqs 4.1-4.6): the shift is v = c(t,R) sqrt(2M_MSH/R), so a lapse factor multiplies sqrt(2m/R); the construction breaks down where M_MSH < 0
the 'escape velocity' / relative-speed reading needs a static observer, so r > 2M
hypothesis_drift: driven.py:212-213 says 'The Gamma = 1 surface IS the PG foliation' without 'in Schwarzschild vacuum'. F1 shows that Gamma = W = 1 is equivalent to an intrinsically flat slicing in ANY spherical spacetime, so the flat-slice ('generalised PG') reading survives in general. The source's PG (geodesic observers starting from rest at infinity) needs Schwarzschild vacuum, or psi = 0 with d_r N = 0 (F2). WEAKENED in wording; exact on the Schwarzschild witness the tree actually uses.

driven.py:390-392 (threshold_speed docstring: 'the Painleve-Gullstrand shift and the local escape velocity') and drivensource.py:175-176 ('sqrt(2m/R) is the Painleve-Gullstrand shift') apply to general Misner-Sharp m. DROPPED hypothesis: unit lapse. By Faraoni-Vachon eq 4.6, MP Sec. IV and F1, the ADM shift is N sqrt(2m/R); only the normal observers' areal velocity equals sqrt(2m/R) for every N. 'Local escape velocity' further needs a static observer (r > 2m) and a conserved Killing energy.

driven.py:205-206 and drivensource.py:180-181 describe 'marginally bound radial free fall ... from rest at infinity'. Outside vacuum, the Gamma = 1 observers are geodesic only if d_r N = 0 (F2), as in LTB dust. With pressure they are accelerated. audits.published_statement: Abstract: 'We construct a particular class of quantum states for a massless, minimally coupled free scalar field which are of the form of a superposition of the vacuum and multi-mode two-particle states ... they can produce an arbitrarily large amount of negative energy in a given region of space at a fixed time. This class of states thus provides an explicit counterexample to the existence of a spatially averaged quantum inequality in four-dimensional spacetime.' Sec. III p.9: 'The first conclusion is the proof that there are no lower bounds on the spatially sampled energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field in four spacetime dimensions. ... S(F) = INT d^3x F(x) <:T00(x,t):> (42) at time t, where F(x) is a spatial sampling function. Let r0 be the characteristic width ... [or] the maximum width of F(x) in any direction.' p.10: 'Thus S(F) is unbounded below. However, this state satisfies the temporal quantum inequality, Eq. (1).' p.8: 'each state in this sequence will have the Hadamard form. By progressively increasing the values of Lambda ... we can make the energy density in our spatially sampled region as negative as we like.' p.10: 'The integration over all space removes the contribution of the rho2 term, leaving only the non-negative contribution of the rho1 term ... the compensating positive energy is arbitrarily far from the negative energy.' p.2: 'the total energy in any quantum state for a quantum field in boundary-free Minkowski spacetime must be non-negative ... <H> >= 0 (3), and <H> = 0 only in the vacuum state' (quoted as a known result, not proven in this paper). p.12 summary: 'we have shown that there are no purely spatially averaged quantum inequalities over bounded regions in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, even though the integral over all space is bounded. We do not know whether it is possible to construct examples in Minkowski space with more severe divergences.'

audits.lacked_data: No measured datum enters FHR. It is a construction in free QFT, so no later measurement can move it. What the authors lacked in 2002 was theory, not data. (a) A rigorous, non-asymptotic proof: the paper works at leading order. This audit's exact-integrand numerics confirm both ln Lambda coefficients (to 1.2e-8 and 1.1e-5), which is evidence FOR the conclusion. (b) Knowledge of other fields: still missing in what was read. Kontou-Sanders Table 3 leaves Maxwell and Dirac at '?', and says the spatial case 'usually' has no QEI. This cuts AGAINST M, because a field-specific spatial bound would be a refusal instrument, not a licence. (c) The UV completion. The divergence is only ln Lambda. If field theory stops at a physical cutoff (Freivogel-Krommydas raise this objection for the null analogue), FHR's family reaches at most K ln(Lambda r0)/r0^4 with K = 1.2554e-2. At r0 = 1 m with a Planck cutoff that is 0.988 hbar c/r0^4, about 104 times the Lorentzian temporal scale at t0 = r0/c. So supplying the missing UV datum would turn 'unbounded below' into a finite, log-enhanced ceiling for this family. That weakens ledger D6's 'THE MAGNITUDE AXIS CARRIES NO NO-GO' and does not help a warp. It does not reverse how bounds.py uses the result: whatever the cutoff, the massless minimally coupled scalar refutes a UNIVERSAL cutoff-free spatial bound. The board's actual refusal is priced on the duration axis (Fewster 1208.5399 Eq.(4)), and FHR's transient witness states obey that bound. The evidence in both directions is computed in the rederive script. Whether a cutoff restores a spatial bound in general is OPEN.

II-III agrees (28/28 checks, including exact-integrand numerics for both log coefficients). Even so, the tree states the result for a larger class than the paper proves. It drops the field restriction to the massless minimally coupled free scalar (bounds.py:31-32, 144-146, 211-216, 262-264; achievable.py:151-153; ledger.py:399-404). It drops state-independence where bounds.py's own S slot makes it load-bearing (bounds.py:262-264, 'FHR prove there cannot be one'). It drops 'Minkowski' at bounds.py:214-215 and achievable.py:152-153/:568. It drops the cutoff-free hypothesis (Lambda -> oo, logarithmic) behind D6's 'magnitude axis carries no no-go' (ledger.py:401-402). The use that matters most still STANDS: no UNIVERSAL spatial bound over a bounded region in 4D Minkowski can refuse the corridor, because one admissible field is a counterexample. The state-independence gap is partly closed here: bounds that depend on the state only through <H> also fail (computed at leading log). The grade is not WRONG: nothing refutes the theorem, and the 'lambda0 > r0' prose and the Eq.(5)/(10) cross-reference are discrepancies, not errors in the conclusion.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners restore the dropped hypotheses (massless minimally coupled scalar, or 'no universal bound'; state-independent; Minkowski; Lambda -> oo), or cited proofs extending FHR to Maxwell, Dirac and massive fields and to curved Cauchy surfaces are READ (Helfer CQG 13 L129 is the named candidate for the curved case). To WRONG: an exact computation showing that the neglected sub-leading terms or N^2 cancel the ln Lambda term (the exact-integrand numerics here make this unlikely), or a proof of a state-independent spatial bound for this field. audits.name: NEC zero RHS saturated by vacuum and by EM field

source.located: No single paper. The pointwise NEC T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 is Hawking & Ellis (CUP 1973) sec. 4.3, which has no arXiv copy (NAMED-NOT-READ). What was read, at source: Kontou & Sanders arXiv:2003.01815 (2020): eq (26) and Table 1 (the NEC), Prop. 2.1, eq (15) (Maxwell/Proca stress tensor), eqs (36)-(37) and Table 2 (Maxwell/Proca: NEC holds for every off-shell configuration; traceless at n=4), eq (39) (non-minimal scalar breaks the NEC classically), and p.3 (every pointwise EC is violated by essentially any QFT, ref [7] = Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe 1965, NAMED-NOT-READ). Martin-Moruno & Visser arXiv:1702.05915 (2017): eq (2.6); type-I table p.6 (NEC <=> rho+p_i>=0); p.4 (non-null EM fields are type I); eq (2.13) (null dust T = f k k); eq (2.15) (electric or magnetic field: diag(mu,-mu,mu,mu)); p.10 (the Casimir vacuum violates all the standard conditions).

audits.published_statement: NEC: 'T_ab k^a k^b >= 0' for every null k (K&S eq 26; MM&V eq 2.6). For a type-I tensor this is rho + p_i >= 0 (MM&V p.6). Maxwell/Proca: the NEC holds 'for all off-shell configurations' (K&S Table 2), and the EM tensor is traceless at n=4 (K&S p.15). MM&V eq (2.15): an electric or magnetic field of energy density mu is diag(mu,-mu,mu,mu), so rho + p_1 = 0. Radiation is T = f k k (eq 2.13). K&S Prop 2.1: if S_ab eta^a xi^b is bounded below, its greatest lower bound is zero. Neither source uses the word 'saturates' here. Saturation, meaning T_kk = 0 at some nonzero null k, is the direct consequence of eqs (2.13) and (2.15) under the sources' own criterion, and this audit re-derives it.
published_hypotheses: Classical, pointwise condition: K&S p.3 says every pointwise EC is violated by essentially any QFT (EGJ, NAMED-NOT-READ); MM&V p.10 says the Casimir vacuum violates all of them

Holds only on a restricted classical matter class. K&S Table 2 has it hold for minimal Klein-Gordon with any V and for Maxwell/Proca; the non-minimal scalar (xi != 0) violates it even on-shell (eq 39)
Maxwell T_ab = F_ac F_b^c - (1/4) g_ab F^2 (K&S eq 15, m=0) in n = 4, where it is traceless
Non-null EM is Hawking-Ellis type I (MM&V p.4); null EM is type II null dust (eq 2.13)
Scale invariance (K&S Prop 2.1): an unnormalised infimum of 0 is trivial, so saturation means T_kk = 0 at a nonzero null k
'Vacuum' means T_ab = 0 (classical, or Minkowski renormalised). Casimir, Boulware, Hartle-Hawking and Unruh vacua VIOLATE the NEC (MM&V p.10)
hypothesis_drift: UNDER-CLAIM IN THE CANONICAL RESTATEMENT, not in the owner. The canonical entry says 'null EM field saturates'. bounds.py:43 and :295 say 'EM' without qualification, and the unqualified form is correct: EVERY Maxwell field saturates at every point, along its principal null direction(s). Non-null: MM&V eq 2.15, checked on 200 random fields (B1, 2.0e-14). Null: eq 2.13 (C1/C2). No effect on K=0.

DROPPED 'classical' AT A DIFFERENT SITE: bounds.py:88-90 (and the printed reading at :406) files the six G=0 bounds, the zero-RHS row among them, as 'statements about quantum field theory on a fixed background'. The pointwise zero-RHS NEC is violated in essentially every QFT (K&S p.3), by Casimir (MM&V p.10), and classically by the non-minimal scalar (K&S eq 39; check F1 gives T_kk = -2). No text at :43 or :295 says 'classical'. Saturation and K=0 are unaffected: the Minkowski vacuum keeps renormalised <T> = 0. Recorded as a discrepancy, not repaired.

IMPLICIT, SATISFIED: slot K ('known to be saturated', bounds.py:28) is undefined. By scaling, every NEC-satisfying T has unnormalised infimum 0 (G1), so saturation must mean attainment at a nonzero k. Vacuum attains it in every direction. EM attains it at every point along its PNDs. A minimal scalar with timelike gradient does not attain it (F2, min 0.49).

IMPLICIT: 'vacuum' at :43/:295 must mean T_ab = 0. Read as a general quantum vacuum, the claim would fail in the other direction, since those vacua violate the NEC (MM&V p.10). Under the reading consistent with the row being a bound that holds, no drift.

**Encoding.** The script checks the real result, not a toy of it. The Maxwell tensor is built from the full covariant F in (-,+,+,+), with F_{0i} = -E_i, F_{ij} = eps_ijk B_k, and T_ab = (F g F^T - 1/4 g F^2)/4pi. That is K&S eq 15 at m=0, Gaussian units. The null vectors are contravariant k = (1, n) with |n| = 1. The principal null directions come from eigenvectors of F^a_b = eta F, so the index placement is consistent. The sign convention is pinned physically: C1/C2 give T_kk = 0 for the +z plane wave (E along x, B along y) at k = (1,0,0,1), with T = l_a l_b/4pi. A sign error would have moved the zero to n = -z.

What the script checks is the pointwise algebraic claim at bounds.py:43/:295:
- T = 0 trivially gives T_kk = 0 for every null k.
- For every 4D Maxwell field, T_kk = |E_perp + n x B|^2/4pi >= 0, and it vanishes along the principal null directions (non-null field) or along l (null field).

Pointwise algebra is the whole content of the claim, so there is no larger theorem the script leaves out.

**Vacuity guards.** Script: vacuity-nec-zero.py. Every check is discriminating; each fails when its hypothesis is negated:
- **V1:** the Groebner test rejects the wrong-sign witness |E_perp - n x B|^2.
- **V2:** without the null constraint |n| = 1, the identity is not a polynomial identity. So the constraint is load-bearing, not decoration.
- **V4:** z3 returns sat on the wrong-sign witness. So the audit's E1 unsat is not vacuous.
- **V6:** the same principal-null-direction test, run on Maxwell plus a small dust term, gives min T_kk/T_00 = 1.3e-2. So B1's 2e-14 measures Maxwell saturation, not a test that returns zero for any tensor.
- **V7:** 100,000 random (F, null k) samples give zero negative values.

**New evidence (V5).** The audit left one gap: z3 asked directly whether T_kk < 0 returned 'unknown'. V5 fixes n = z, which loses nothing because of rotation invariance (a named hypothesis), and z3 then returns unsat for T_kk < 0. That is a direct machine check of non-negativity, alongside the sum-of-squares route.

**V3 is informational, not a refutation.** Dropping the -1/4 g F^2 term leaves T_kk unchanged, because g_kk = 0. So that part of the hypothesis "Maxwell T_ab, traceless at n=4" carries no load for this claim. Tracelessness is not needed for saturation. The audit does not say it is load-bearing, so nothing in it is wrong.

**Two minor findings, recorded and not repaired. Neither moves the grade.**
1. The citation "bounds.py:88-90" is slightly off. The 'statements about quantum field theory on a fixed background' sentence is at :90, inside the paragraph at :89-91. The printed version at :406 is cited correctly.

**Grade.** STANDS is supported: the script reproduces, the encoding is faithful, every check is non-vacuous, and V5 now closes the one solver gap.

source.located: No single source paper. The tree derives this itself in drivensource.py sec.4 and obligation E2, building on the classical charged-body and Reissner-Nordstrom literature. The external result that bears directly on the universal claim is Bonnor & Cooperstock, 'Does the electron contain negative mass?', Phys. Lett. A 139 (1989) 442, together with Cooperstock & Rosen 1989 and Herrera & Varela, Phys. Lett. A 189 (1994) 11. These are pre-arXiv and NAMED-NOT-READ. They are restated exactly in arXiv:0710.5619 (S. Bhadra, PhD thesis 2007) sec. 3.1-3.2.1, eqs (3.1),(3.5)-(3.7), pp. 34-36, and summarized on pp. 17-18 (with Ponce de Leon 1988 and Lopez 1992). The equality case (source boundary exactly at r = e^2/2m, zero bare mass) is restated in arXiv:1212.2920 (Burinskii 2013) eq (5), p.3, the Lopez bubble. Measured lepton sizes come from arXiv:2506.02450 (Bourilkov 2025) Table 1 and eq (3), which draw on L3 PLB 489 (2000) 81 and Bourilkov PRD 62 (2000) 076005.

audits.published_statement: Bonnor-Cooperstock 1989, as restated in arXiv:0710.5619 p.36: 'any spherically symmetric distribution of charged fluid, irrespective of its equation of state, whose total mass, radius and charge correspond to the observed values of the electron, must have a negative energy distribution (at least for some values of the radial coordinate)'. The mechanism is in eqs (3.5)-(3.7). Match e^{-2lambda} = 1 - (1/r) int_0^r (8 pi rho + e^{-(nu+lambda)} E^2) r^2 dr to Reissner-Nordstrom at r = a. With m = 6.76e-56 cm, q = 1.38e-34 cm and a = 1e-16 cm, q^2/a^2 - 2m/a ~ 2e-36 > 0, so rho < 0 somewhere. Eq (3.1), M = m - q^2/2a, comes out negative, about -1e-52 cm. Ponce de Leon 1988 (restated p.21): repulsion 'always takes place in the interior of a charged perfect fluid sphere when its radius is less than the classical electron radius', but not necessarily for anisotropic spheres or charge sitting on the boundary. The tree's bound r_c <= a is the contrapositive of this result, since r_c <= a holds exactly when the Misner-Sharp mass at the surface, m_MS(a), is >= 0. The literature applies it to the electron in the opposite direction: the measured a is below r_c, so the interior must hold negative mass.
published_hypotheses: Classical Einstein-Maxwell (GR with linear Maxwell), static, spherically symmetric charged fluid (0710.5619 eqs 3.3-3.6)
Regular centre: the mass integral starts at r = 0 with no point singularity (eq 3.5)
Reissner-Nordstrom exterior matched at a sharp boundary r = a
Inputs: electron m and q in geometrized units, and the 1983 size bound a ~ 1e-16 cm (Quigg 1983)
Spin and magnetic moment are not modelled (0710.5619 p.35)

The tree's derivation (drivensource.py:144-150) uses flat-space accounting, M >= X/a, and holds 'whenever the body's own contribution to M is non-negative'. E2 (drivensource.py:426-429) states this as the hypothesis mu >= 0.

The tree uses it more widely than it holds, in two ways:

The measured electron (ratio 5032) and muon (28) violate it under the classical Einstein-Maxwell reading that the derivation itself uses. I could not refute the NARROWED grade in either direction. I checked it against the sources, the tree and my own computations.

TREE. I re-read overturn.py:48-53, 256-266 and 360-380, and drivensource.py:113-170 and 346-440. git diff 3223791..314f04d shows neither file changed. overturn.py:49-51 says "any body of charge Q and mass M >= 0 ... for every charged body that exists". overturn.py:376 says "every charged body with mass >= 0". drivensource.py:149 and obligation E2 at :427-429 use mu >= 0, the bare mass, and E2's own DRIFT guard at :430-433 shows the bound fails without it. The M-vs-mu weakening is real. It is a paraphrase drift and not a misprint of an external result. It also is not the only reason for NARROWED: the empirical universal "every charged body that exists" is declared with no table of bodies, and that alone supports the grade.

SOURCES, read myself through alphaXiv:
- arXiv:0710.5619, pp.34-36. It restates Bonnor-Cooperstock 1989 and Cooperstock-Rosen 1989 exactly as the audit quotes: the "any spherically symmetric distribution of charged fluid, irrespective of its equation of state" sentence, eqs (3.1) and (3.5)-(3.7), and the inputs m = 6.76e-56 cm, q = 1.38e-34 cm, a = 1e-16 cm (Quigg 1983). Page 17 gives Ponce de Leon 1988 with the anisotropic and boundary-charge caveats. The originals stay NAMED-NOT-READ, as the audit says.
- arXiv:2506.02450, Table 1 and eq (3). The bounds are electron 2.8e-19 m, muon 2.4e-19 m and tau 4.0e-19 m (95% CL), with the stated factor sqrt2 when F_e = 1. All quoted correctly.

COMPUTATIONS. I re-ran the auditor's script: exit 0, all checks pass. Independently I get r_c = alpha*hbar*c/(2Mc^2), and r_c/a_max = 5032 for the electron, 28.4 for the muon and 1.01 for the tau (0.72 with the sqrt2 factor). The B-C values come out as eq (3.7) = 1.903e-36 and eq (3.1) = -9.5e-53 cm, and mu = -2571 MeV. The contrapositive reading is correct: q^2/a^2 - 2m/a > 0 holds exactly when r_c > a.

The full-GR thin shell is mu(2a - mu)/(2a), and the audit flags one way it can fail: a branch with mu > 2a. I checked whether that branch is a real escape and it is not. For the electron's numbers the two roots are mu = -3.40e-54 m (the -2571 MeV body) and mu = 2a = 5.6e-19 m. The second has junction sign 1 - mu/a = -1. The electron's field is far past extremal (Q/M = 2.0e21), so Reissner-Nordstrom has no horizon, no throat and no second asymptotically flat sheet. The "exterior" of that branch is therefore the r < a region around the naked singularity, not a body seen from infinity. So for any static shell with an asymptotically flat exterior, mu >= 0 still forces r_c <= a. This strengthens the conditional half.

WHY NOT A DIFFERENT GRADE.
- STANDS: no. The tree's wording has a z3 counterexample (mu = -1, M = 1, r_c = 2a). The electron and muon violate the universal under the very classical Einstein-Maxwell reading the derivation uses, and the read source makes the same point.
- WRONG: no. The conditional theorem is sound. The lepton counterexample needs a quantum pointlike particle to be treated as a classical body whose radius is its form-factor bound.
- DATA-DEPENDENT: no. No plausible data move flips either half.
- OPEN: no. The conditional is machine-checked, and the composite bodies pass by 2 to 11 orders of magnitude.

DISCREPANCIES. Recorded only; none of them moves the grade.
(1) The audit leaves the tau OPEN using Table 1 alone. Table 3 of the same paper, which the audit read (pp.1-5), gives a contact-interaction bound of 1.4e-19 m, so r_c/a = 2.9. Table 2 gives 1.2e-20 m, so 34. Both depend on an assumed coupling, so OPEN is defensible, but the tau is closer to a third counterexample than the audit says. The electron's (g-2) bound of 3.2e-19 m (quadratic scaling) gives about 4400, consistent with Table 1.
(2) The audit says L2's "EMPTY" may survive only "by a quantum argument the tree does not make". That understates it. By the audit's own identity (D), a classical electron with r_c > a has mu < 0, meaning negative matter energy somewhere. That is exactly what L2 says negative m(r) requires, so the electron does not give a route that avoids negative energy even classically. This affects what rests on the result (rests_on_it), not the grade.
(3) The peripheral eq (9)/(11) discrepancy in 2603.22223 was not re-read. It is irrelevant to the grade.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run script_path from a copy, check the encoding against the published statement, run vacuity guards
verifiers.reason:
I copied the audit's script to verify/rederive/ and re-ran it. It exits 0 with ALL CHECKS PASS, and every number matches the audit: E2 is unsat; the M>0 wording is sat with witness X=2, a=1, mu=-1, M=1, r_c=2; the shell excess is mu(2a-mu)/(2a); the measured ratios are electron 5032, muon 28.4, tau 1.01 (0.72 if the electron is taken as pointlike); Bonnor-Cooperstock eq (3.7) comes out 1.903e-36 and eq (3.1) -9.5e-53 cm.

ENCODING. Check A is a toy, not the theorem. It encodes the tree's own E2 verbatim, which uses flat-space accounting M = mu + X/a. Check C is exact GR, but only for a thin shell. I confirmed its Israel relation independently: f_out(M) - (1 - mu/a)^2 simplifies to 0 at M = mu - mu^2/2a + Q^2/2a. Check D is a purely algebraic equivalence.

To see whether the conditional result holds beyond these toys, I derived the general static spherical case from scratch with a sympy Christoffel-to-Ricci computation. It gives G^t_t = -2m'/r^2, so m' = 4 pi r^2 rho + q^2/(2r^2). With a regular centre, m(0) = 0, this gives M - Q^2/2a = int_0^a (4 pi r^2 rho + q^2/2r^2) dr. That is >= 0 whenever rho >= 0, and strictly positive once charge sits inside the body. For example, a uniform charged sphere has r_c/a = 15Q^2/(2(9Q^2 + 20 pi a^4 rho0)), which is 5/6 at rho0 = 0.

So the conditional theorem holds in full GR for any static, spherically symmetric body with a regular centre, rho >= 0 and the area radius increasing outward (no throat), not only for the shell. That supports the audit's 'conditional STANDS' half more strongly than the audit itself showed.

VACUITY.
- Each hypothesis set is satisfiable: A with mu >= 0 is sat, C on the normal branch is sat, and C's equality guard at mu = 0 is sat.
- Negating mu >= 0 gives counterexamples. In A, mu < 0 with M > 0 always breaks the bound: requiring the bound to hold returns unsat. In C, u < 0 breaks it (sat).
- In the general form, a negative rho0 = -Q^2/(4 pi a^4) gives r_c/a = 15/8 > 1, which is the Bonnor-Cooperstock mechanism.
None of the checks passes with its hypotheses negated, so none is vacuous.

REFINEMENTS, none of which changes the grade:
1. In GR the correct named hypothesis is local rho >= 0 plus a regular centre plus no throat. 'mu >= 0' is the flat-space proxy for it.
2. The audit says the shell bound fails 'only for mu > 2a, on the far sheet'. That is right: for a < mu <= 2a the bound still holds (negation unsat). But it means the tree's E2 also leaves out a needed hypothesis (normal branch, i.e. no throat). The audit files this as 'DROPPED, harmless'. It is harmless only because a far-sheet shell is not an ordinary existing body, and it should still be a named hypothesis.
3. The electron and muon counterexamples hold only if a LEP form-factor bound is read as a sharp classical radius. The audit already says so.

Peripheral check G, on arXiv:2603.22223, reproduces: the integral of eq (9) as printed is m_f + pi alpha/16R. The audit correctly records this as a discrepancy, not a refutation.

Overall: the conditional theorem stands, and is wider than the audit showed. The tree's use of it is wider than what holds, in two ways: it weakens the hypothesis to M >= 0, which has a counterexample, and it asserts an empirical universal over 'every charged body that exists' with no table of bodies, which the electron and muon contradict under the classical reading. NARROWED is supported.

R2-H4 Implicit in the alpha coefficient: the isomer and ground state differ in Coulomb energy by 2e5 x 7 eV = 1.4 MeV.

Three data have arrived since: w measured at 8.355733554 eV (2024); a measured-input K_alpha = 5900(2300), backed by theory giving 1e3-1e4 (2024-26); and sigma-term values of 59.1 vs 43.7 MeV for sigma_piN and 28.6 MeV for sigma_s.

Evidence for M's hypothesis: eq. (9)'s alpha coefficient is 28x (20-47x) too large, so the missing Q0 and <r^2> data moved it by more than an order of magnitude. The (7 eV/w) factor also moved, by 16%.

Evidence against, or limiting it: the author called eq. (9) 'a rough estimate' and carried a factor-2.2 uncertainty in w, so this is an estimate overtaken by data, not an established result shown false. The X_q and X_s coefficients, which carry the tree's figure, are still unmeasured. The X_q estimates scatter in both directions (Flambaum-Wiringa is 3.3x higher), and no later X_s computation was found. R1 is unmoved: it is exact in the chiral limit, and the quark-mass correction is the S the tree already adds.

Effect on the tree: eps_det changes by x1.19 from the new w, and possibly up to about x10 if the enhancement is ~1e4. The H2 density changes by x0.64-1.29 from S. As far as computed here, none of these moves an order-of-magnitude verdict.
audits.grade_evidence:
R1 stands as the chiral-limit proportionality. The tree's extension to f = S is checked exact in sympy. The 'Lambda fixed' premise is the tree's own named hypothesis resting on Flambaum's citation (address.py:446 and :104). Its datum S is contested, and moving it changes the H2 density by x0.64-1.29 but not the verdict.

R2 controls the grade. The transcription is exact and the tree's coefficients are reproduced to 1e-12, but the conclusion moves with data that have moved:
(i) w is now measured at 8.3557 eV, against the 7 eV the tree uses (address.py:763). That changes eps_det from 2.86e-24 to 3.41e-24.
(ii) The alpha coefficient is 28x the measured K = 5900(2300), backed by 1e3-1e4 from theory. This term is only 1e-3 of the tree's figure.
(iii) The X_q and X_s coefficients that carry the figure are unmeasured and contested. If the strong enhancement is ~1e4, eps_det rises 10x.

Why not WRONG: the author called eq. (9) a rough estimate, and no counterexample to the strong-sector terms is shown. Why not STANDS: a datum has moved and the controlling coefficients are contested. The tree's claim that section 9 does not depend on this value was not re-verified here.

I read the source myself (alphaXiv, 0705.3704v2, all 8 pages). R1 on p.4 and R2 on p.5 (eq. 9, with the energies 3.5±1, 5.5±1 and 7.6±0.5 eV at refs [51]-[53]) are transcribed verbatim. The tree's constants at address.py:761-764 match eq. (9) exactly, and the auditor's hypothesis list matches the text. One small imprecision: 'model dependent' on p.3 qualifies the 35 in eq. (2), not the 34 for Lambda. It does not affect the grade.

The grade survives every attempt I made on it in either direction.

(1) The arithmetic is correct. I re-ran rederive/0705.3704.py and every check passes. I also checked independently:
- w = nu·h/e = 8.355733554 eV.
- The coefficient at w is -2.929e5, giving eps_det = 3.414e-24.
- 2e5·7/8.3557/5900 = 28.4.
- The X_q estimates re-normalised to the measured w are 3.638e4, 6.367e4 and 1.364e5. I read these in Flambaum-Wiringa 0807.4943 itself: p.3 eq. (7) gives 1.5e5 at 7.6 eV and compares it with 0.4e5 [3] and 0.7e5 [23]. p.1 excludes the strange quark for 'larger uncertainty' and states 'convenient to assume that Lambda_QCD is constant'. The conclusion on p.7 says 'not better than a factor of 2'.
- Beeks 2407.17300 p.3 eqs (8)-(10) give Delta E_C = 0.049(19) MeV and K = 5900(2300). p.1-2 give nu = 2 020 407 384 335(2) kHz.
- address.py and excite.py never mention 8.3557 eV. The only hits are in docket67-raw copies of this audit.

(2) The case for WRONG fails. A WRONG grade would rest on the alpha term being 28x too large. But Beeks's K is not measured. It is a prolate-spheroid model fed with measured Delta Q0/Q0 and Delta<r^2>, and the octupole term is unquantified: Beeks p.4 says a 1% differential change in beta_3 moves K by 2850. On a linear extrapolation, reaching 1.68e5 would need roughly a 56% differential beta_3, so the term is overtaken but not formally refuted. The source also labels eq. (9) 'a rough estimate'. The strong-sector X_q and X_s terms carry 99.9% of the tree's coefficient, and they remain unmeasured and contested both ways: FW is 3.3x higher, Caputo argues about 1e4. Supporting point the audit missed: FW 0807.4943 p.4 restates He-Ren 2007 as giving an alpha enhancement of 4e3 (Delta E_C 0.03 MeV). So the eq. (9) alpha term was already contested within months of the review, not only by the 2024 data.

(3) The case for STANDS or NARROWED also fails, though I did meet the audit's own condition for 'toward NARROWED'. I imported address.py read-only and re-evaluated th229_coefficient at the measured w, scaling the enhancement over 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 and 1e6. In every case:
- the section-9 domination ratio stays finite and monotone increasing in rho, spanning 1.3e5 to 3.3e6;
- the courier beats the electronic one;
- the threshold source density stays above osmium (12x to 1.2e4x).
So the tree's claim at address.py:294-295, 'section 9's verdict does not depend on its value', is now computed over that range rather than merely asserted. That settles the tree's verdict, not the external result. Eq. (9)'s own coefficients have moved with data (w by x0.8377, the alpha term about 28x) or stay data-contingent (X_q spread 3.75x; X_s unmeasured). The figure the tree prints, '2.86e-24 ... EIGHT ORDERS BETTER', moves by x1.19 from the new w and by up to x10 (to seven orders) if the enhancement is about 1e4. A printed figure that moves with data, under a verdict that does not, is what DATA-DEPENDENT means. NARROWED would wrongly imply that eq. (9) holds within a reduced scope.

Two precision corrections, neither of which changes the grade:
(a) Where the audit says 'measured K' or 'the measured value' (data_at_publication, grade_evidence), it should read 'K extracted by geometric model from measured Delta Q0/Q0 and Delta<r^2>, octupole unquantified'. The lacked_data field already words it correctly.
(b) The audit's 'not re-verified' caveat on section 9 can now be replaced by the computation in verify/refute/r_0705.3704_sec9.out, for the range 1e3 to 1e6 at the measured w, H1, S = 0.06.

SOURCE RE-READ (alphaXiv, 0705.3704v2):
- p.4 states R1 verbatim.
- p.5 eq. (9) matches the audit's transcription: 10^5 (2 da/a + 0.5 dX_q/X_q - 5 dX_s/X_s)(7 eV/w), called 'A rough estimate'. The 3.5/5.5/7.6 eV energies are as quoted.
- The tree's TH229_* constants (address.py:761-763) and th229_coefficient (address.py:776-785) match that equation.
- Flambaum-Wiringa 0807.4943, also read: p.3 eq. (7) gives 1.5e5 at 7.6 eV and quotes 0.4e5 (Flambaum 2006) and 0.7e5 (He-Ren); p.1 excludes the strange-quark term for 'larger uncertainty'; p.7 says the coefficient is not known better than a factor of 2.
- Beeks 2407.17300, also read: p.3 eqs (8)-(10) give Delta E_C = 0.049(19) MeV and K = 5900(2300), and p.1 gives nu = 2 020 407 384 335(2) kHz.
- So every external input the script uses is as READ.

ENCODING. The R2 checks are the real computation, not a toy of it: eq. (9) evaluated with the tree's d ln X/d ln v.

The R1 check in sympy is the Feynman-Hellmann chain rule. It is an identity by construction, but that is exactly what the audit claims for it: with Lambda fixed, d ln m_p/d ln v = S, and Flambaum's statement is the S -> 0 limit.

VACUITY GUARD (verify/rederive/vacuity_0705.3704.py):
- V1. I let Lambda vary with v, which negates H2. The sympy identity then fails: the difference is non-zero. The result reduces exactly to the tree's H1 form, ell(1-S) + S (address.py:507). So the check is not vacuous.
- V2. The script reproduces the H1 coefficient using the tree's own K_alpha on both sides, so that comparison is circular. To close the gap I recomputed K_alpha(H1) independently from the textbook b_i and w_l = 2/9, giving 1.849653e-3. That matches the tree exactly, and so does the H1 coefficient, -3.496301e5.
- V3 shows why V2 was needed: the script's own comparison still passes after I injected a 2x error into K_alpha, because both sides move together. The coefficient itself moves by only 1.06e-3, so the circular check could not catch it.
- V4. The check 'nuclear courier beats the electronic one by >1e3' reduces to |coeff| > 1e3, since gain = |c|. It passes at an enhancement of 1e3 and fails at 1e2. It is not vacuous, but it is weak, and it does not test the tree's section-9 claim. The audit says so itself ('NOT re-verified').
- V5. The osmium density check fails only for S > 0.975, so across any physical S it can only pass. It confirms the arithmetic and little else.

MINOR (does not change the grade):
1. The audit lists the S span as 0.0466-0.0935. Its lower end, 43.7/938, is light quarks only. Yet the audit's own DROPPED-DATUM argues that under H2 the strange sigma term belongs in S. With the strange term included, the lower end at 1 sigma is about 0.067. The quoted span is therefore wider than the audit's premise supports. It errs on the conservative side, and the verdict does not move either way.
2. FW 0807.4943 p.4 records He-Ren 2007's direct calculation of the alpha enhancement as 4e3 (Delta E_C 0.03 MeV). That was already pointing against eq. (9)'s 2e5 by 2008, and the audit's later_literature omits it. Adding it would strengthen the audit's alpha-coefficient finding, not weaken it.

GRADE. DATA-DEPENDENT is what the evidence supports:
- The transcription is exact.
- w has moved from 7 eV to 8.3557 eV. That rescales the tree's figure by 0.8377, taking eps_det(H1) from 2.86e-24 to 3.41e-24.
- The alpha term is 28x the Beeks K. Beeks gets K from a prolate-spheroid model, and the octupole contribution is unquantified.
- The controlling X_q and X_s coefficients are unmeasured and the published estimates disagree.
- WRONG is not supported: the author called eq. (9) a rough estimate, and nothing shows the strong-sector terms are false. STANDS is not supported, because a datum has moved.

The data claims hold at source. I found one misattribution and one overstatement, and neither moves the grade.

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE
- value_then, 0705.3704 p.5: 3.5+-1 eV [51], 5.5+-1 eV [52] and 7.6+-0.5 eV [53]. Eq. (9) is verbatim, called 'a rough estimate', and attributed to Ref. [38]. R1 is verbatim on p.4.
- value_now for w, 2407.17300 p.1-2: nu = 2 020 407 384 335(2) kHz. Using the exact h/e this gives 8.355733554 eV, and 7/w = 0.837748.
- Alpha row, 2407.17300 eqs. 8-10: Delta E_C = 0.049(19) MeV, K = 5900(2300), Delta Q0/Q0 = 1.791(2)%. A 1% differential octupole change moves K by 2850, and the octupole contribution is unquantified (p.4).
- Recomputed: 2e5 x 7/w = 1.6755e5. That is 28.40x the measured K, or 20.43x to 46.54x within 1 sigma. The audit's figures are right.
- X_q row, 0807.4943 p.1 and p.3 eq. (7):
  - 1.5e5 at 7.6 eV, compared with 0.4e5 (Ref. [3] = Flambaum 2006) and 0.7e5 (He-Ren), both rescaled to 7.6 eV.
  - Accuracy 'no better than a factor of 2' (p.7). The strange quark is excluded for 'larger uncertainty' (p.1). 'Convenient to assume that Lambda_QCD is constant' (p.1).
  - Normalised to w: 1.3643e5, 3.638e4 and 6.367e4, against eq. (9)'s 4.189e4. The spread is 3.75x, and FW/eq. (9) = 3.26x at 7.6 eV. All as stated.
- Sigma terms:
  - sigma_piN = 59.1(3.5) MeV (1506.04142 eq. 21).
  - 43.7(3.6) MeV and sigma_s = 28.6(9.3) MeV (2303.08741 abstract, eq. 30).
  - The S span of 0.0466 to 0.0935 and the H2 density factors of x0.64 to x1.29 follow arithmetically.
- moves_conclusion follows in every row. The w shift is x0.8377 on the coefficient. The alpha term carries 1.06e-3 of the bracket under H1 and 0 under H2. The X_s row is honestly OPEN.

DISCREPANCY 1 (attribution, not a refutation)
- 2303.08741 p.5 and Fig. 3 put the 2.4 sigma tension against the isospin-corrected dispersive value of 55.9(3.5) MeV, not 59.1.
- 59.1 vs 43.7 is 3.07 sigma (computed). The audit's data row and later_literature row both pair '59.1' with '2.4 sigma'.
- The rederive script does carry the 55.9 row.
- The tree's own 0.06 is labelled 'sigma_piN ~ 56 MeV' (address.py:452), and 55.9/m_p = 0.0596.

DISCREPANCY 2 (lacked_data: the evidence for M's hypothesis is overstated)
- The audit says 'the missing Q0 and <r^2> data moved it [the alpha coefficient] by more than an order of magnitude'.
- But 0807.4943 p.3-4, which the audit cites but does not quote on this point:
  - calls 1.3 MeV (from neutron removal) 'an upper estimate (and a natural scale)' and says 'one should expect a fraction of MeV';
  - reports He-Ren 2007's direct calculation as an alpha enhancement of 4e3, or Delta E_C = 0.03 MeV. At the measured w that is 3.6e3, within 1 sigma of Beeks' 5900(2300).
- So the right order of K_alpha was reached by theory in 2007, with no measured Q0 or <r^2>. The 2024 data chose between estimates that already existed; it did not reveal an error nobody could have seen.
- That supports the audit's own 'evidence against' (eq. (9)'s alpha term was a rough upper scale, overtaken rather than wrong), and it weakens 'evidence for'. Both sides of M's hypothesis are still answered with evidence, not presumed. Only the weight of the 'for' side should be reduced.

GRADE
DATA-DEPENDENT stands. R2's controlling X_q and X_s coefficients are unmeasured and contested, w has moved by 16%, and R1 is unmoved. The audit should:
- correct the 2.4 sigma pairing;
- add He-Ren 2007's alpha 4e3 and FW's 'upper estimate' wording to later_literature and lacked_data;
- leave the grade unchanged.

verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the NARROWED grade in either direction. The grade mainly rests on its point (1), and I checked that point on my own.

(1) Monotonicity is false near threshold. In sympy, d/drho[sqrt(rho)/ln(B rho)] times sqrt(rho) ln^2 equals ln(B rho)/2 - 1. So r/d falls whenever eps0 is between eps_det and e^2 eps_det. I computed address.domination_ratio myself, which is the tree's own function (f = 0.26889, H1, S = 0.06):
- domination_ratio(9.828e11) = 1.824e24, while domination_ratio(2.457e12) = 4.784e23.
- The sampled minimum sits at rho/rho_th = 7.4, against e^2 = 7.389, for both eps_det = 1e-18 and 2.86e-24.

The section-9 prose says 'EVERY INCREASE IN THE SOURCE WIDENS IT' and 'it is monotone'. That is a false mathematical claim on a nonempty window, not a misprint, so it is a real narrowing of the stated scope. This does not push the grade to WRONG:
- The asymptotic claim stands.
- The Role 1 verdict stands: the minimum ratio over excite's scan is 6.98e23.
- excite.py:1563-1569 already records the near-threshold regime.
- STANDS would also be wrong, because the address.py text that excite cites at :173 holds on a smaller class than it states.

(4) The factor 2 in the surface amplitude checks out (sympy):
- Planar sharp edge: exterior amplitude = e0/2.
- Exact sphere: surface/e0 = (mR cosh mR - sinh mR) e^{-mR}/(mR), whose limit is 1/2.
The overstatement favours the Higgs, so it is a conservative discrepancy, as the audit says.

(2) The collapse density is confirmed: 3c^2/(8 pi G) = 1.607e26 kg/m^3 at R = 1 m.

I read Shi arXiv:2107.04206v1 at source and confirmed M_c ~ 2.7e14 a_m^2 kg. It uses valence quarks only, with m_f = 3.45 MeV, so f = 0.011 and the rescale by 24.4 to 1.1e13 is correct.

Minor inaccuracies in the audit. None of them moves the grade:
(a) It says the M_c statement is on p.14. It is on p.15.
(b) 'CONTESTED for the SM doublet' overstates Shi. Shi applies the real-scalar results to the Higgs 'for order-of-magnitude estimations' and only flags 'additional effects due to the non-abelian group' (p.14).
(c) The audit omits a point that cuts toward the tree. In Shi's convention (A >= 0), the q(inf) = -1 configuration is the unique ground state, labelled N-- = 1 in phase 1210, and it has no light horizon. The light-horizon branches are q(inf) = +1 'excited states'. So the 'perturbative-branch' hypothesis concerns which state is occupied, not whether the perturbative solution exists.
(d) 'Its decade grid does not sample the window' is slightly wrong for address.py's selftest. The selftest uses eps_det = e229 = 2.860e-24, where the window is rho = 2.34e6 to 1.73e7. The data-sensitivity claims are consistent with my checks: every moved input enters under a log or a square root.

Overall, NARROWED is supported. It is neither over-represented against the tree (the verdict is untouched) nor in its favour (the printed monotonicity is computably false).

verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade holds up on re-run. Three of the audit's supporting sentences are wrong or imprecise, and none of them moves the grade.

RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It exits 0 and its numbers match the audit:
- counterexample 1.8232e24 -> 4.7840e23
- minimum over excite's scan 6.978e23
- worst case 8.099e20
- collapse density 1.607e26, where r/d = 1.292e29

It prints 16 PASS lines, not 17. The audit's "17" comes from grep -c PASS on the .out file, which also counts the line "RESULT: ALL ARITHMETIC CHECKS PASS". That is a miscount, not a failure.

ENCODING. C3 and C4 encode the tree's own functions exactly. address.higgs_range is lambda_h ln(eps0/eps_det) with eps0 proportional to rho, and newton_range grows as sqrt(rho). So the sympy form A sqrt(rho)/ln(B rho) is the theorem as published, not a simplified model of it. One caveat: C4's "independent" recomputation re-codes the formulas but takes G, hbar, M_HIGGS and vev from higgs.py. So it checks that the formulas were assembled correctly, not the constants.

I also checked whether the theorem means r/d or r - d. The audit reads "EVERY INCREASE IN THE SOURCE WIDENS IT" as a claim about r/d. If "the gap" meant r - d, the claim would be true everywhere: my check V3 shows r - d is monotone across the threshold window. But the next line, ":320 it is monotone", and address.py's own selftest, which asserts "AND IT IS MONOTONE INCREASING IN rho" on domination_ratio, show the tree means the ratio. So the drift item stands, and the counterexample is real.

VACUITY GUARD (script adt-vacuity.py):
- V1: replace gravity with a massive mediator of logarithmic range. Excite's "monotone from 1e14" check fails, and so does "min > 1e20" (minimum 1.35e18).
- V2: replace the Higgs with an unscreened field. The sympy limit becomes 0, not infinity.

So the checks can tell the theorem from its negation; they are not vacuous.

ERRORS IN THE AUDIT (all minor):
(a) The edge-amplitude item says "every excite check still passes". That is false. With the eps0/2 edge amplitude, the Higgs range at rho = 1e12 is 0 (ds[0] = 0). Excite's CONTROL "the Higgs standoff itself does grow, all > 0" then FAILS, and so does "equal steps per decade". Only the three domination checks still pass. The discrepancy is still conservative for the verdict.
(b) The audit says address.py's selftest "passes only because its decade grid does not sample the window". That is imprecise. With eps_det = 2.86e-24 the window is 2.34e6 to 1.73e7, and the grid point 1e7 lies inside it. The selftest passes because 1e7 sits below the minimum at e^2 times threshold and the next point, 1e8, is past it. Its ratio (8.93e20) is still above the ratio at 1e7 (7.31e20), so no falling pair of samples is ever compared.
(c) The "worst case 8.1e20" is the minimum over the six scan points only. The true minimum is at eps0 = e^2 eps_det, where r/d = r/(2 lambda_h). At R = 1 m that minimum is 2.07e19. Letting R range from 1 mm to 100 m it falls to 6.6e14 (R = 1 mm, H1, S = 0.106, floor 1e-6, eps_det = 2.86e-24). Both are still far above 1, so the verdict and the DATA-DEPENDENT threshold argument survive. The audit's figure is a grid statement and should say so.

WHAT STANDS. C1 is the linear response with only m_h^2 entering. C2's planar sharp-edge solution is a fair reduction of the sphere for R >> lambda_h. C3's derivative sign is ln(B rho) - 2. C6's collapse density is 3c^2/(8 pi G R^2). All re-derive correctly.

Not re-checked under this lens: C8's inputs taken from Shi 2107.04206 (M_c, the 1.3e22 normalisation, the light-horizon formula) and the papers themselves. Their status is unchanged by this check.

Section 9's "every increase widens it / it is monotone" is false on (eps_det, e^2 eps_det), and "without bound" needs the weak field and the perturbative branch. audits.name: Closed curves in a free translation-lattice quotient lift to curves from p to p + V, V in L (covering-space lifting). With the reduction lemma this gives: a closed causal curve exists in R^{1,d}/L iff L contains a nonzero causal vector.

source.located: There is no single source paper. The lift is the path-lifting and deck-transformation property of covering maps (Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Prop. 1.30 and Prop. 1.40). Hatcher has no arXiv copy and is NAMED-NOT-READ. Its physics restatement for spacetime quotients was READ in two papers: Hubeny, Rangamani & Ross, arXiv:hep-th/0307257v3 (2003), Sect. 2.2 and 5.2; and Greene, Kabat, Levin & Porrati (the GKLP of latticectc.py:23,35), arXiv:2208.09014v3, pp. 1-3. Also READ: arXiv:2206.13590v2 Sect. 2.1, for the covering-space image picture, and Minguzzi arXiv:1709.06494v4 Def. 2.13 and 2.23, for the definitions of causal and stably causal.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-th/0307257, 2208.09014, 2206.13590 and 1709.06494, each returning page text. The lemma is read only as HRR and GKLP apply it. HRR Sect. 5.2: 'we will identify some point q ... with the point p. But q is in the future of p ... thus giving us a CTC'. HRR Sect. 2.2: a time function on M/G pulls back to a G-invariant one. GKLP p. 3: 'In the covering space, image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones.'

audits.published_statement:
Topology (Hatcher Prop. 1.30, NAMED-NOT-READ, restated in the papers read): every path lifts uniquely through a covering map once its initial point is fixed. For X = X~/G under a properly discontinuous action, a loop at [x] lifts to a path from x to g x with g in G, and G = pi_1(X) when X~ is simply connected.

HRR hep-th/0307257 Sect. 5.2: identifying p with a point q in its future gives a CTC. HRR Sect. 2.2: 'M/G is itself stably causal iff there exists a time function tau on M such that L_xi tau = 0'.

GKLP 2208.09014 p. 3: no CTC arises because identified image points are mutually outside each other's light cones.

The tree's combined form, latticectc.py:25-26: '(a) A closed causal curve exists in the quotient IFF L contains a nonzero causal vector.'
published_hypotheses: Covering-space action: the group acts properly discontinuously. For translations of R^{1,d} this is the same as L being a discrete subgroup; acting freely is not sufficient.
Paths are continuous, and the lift is unique once its initial point is fixed.
The covering space is simply connected, so that the deck group equals pi_1. R^{1,d} is simply connected.
HRR Sect. 2.2: M is stably causal and G is generated by a Killing vector. The pull-back proof does not use that restriction.
HRR Sect. 5.2: the identified point q lies in I+(p). This is a sufficient condition, stated for the plane wave.

GKLP: flat M^4 x S^1 with one spatial identification (rank 1). The argument on p. 3 is offered as a 'quick argument'; the detailed no-CTC result (Sect. 4) is computed for round-trip signals on the brane.
hypothesis_drift: latticectc.py:21 and :112-118 read 'rank-n TRANSLATION lattice L acting freely'. This is a wording issue, not a narrowing. Every nonzero translation acts freely, so 'acting freely' adds nothing. The hypothesis the lift actually needs is that L is discrete, and only the word 'lattice' carries it. The code cannot leave that class: every generator is an exact Fraction, and the Z-span of rational vectors is discrete. The boundary example (1,1,s),(0,0,1) is R-independent, so it is discrete too.

latticectc.py:18-32: the covering-space lemma is used but never stated or cited (canonical status_word: 'none'). HRR 2003 already uses the lift-to-image argument for quotients and is not cited. This is an attribution gap, not a mathematical one.

latticectc.py:27-32 and :251-280: the reduction lemma is proved only for chains of K piecewise-linear legs (z3 at K = 1, 2; up to 4 with --full). The step to an arbitrary causal curve is not written: the curve's displacement is an integral of tangents that lie in the closed convex future cone, so it lies in that cone. The step follows from the convexity the tree does prove. The gap is in the written proof, not in the conclusion.

latticectc.py:29-31 and :283-300 claim cone convexity 'in any dimension', but the Lagrange identity is machine-checked only at spatial dimension 3, and the premise dot <= ab is assumed rather than derived. Re-derivation L4 checks the identity at dimensions 1-8, and L2 derives the lemma from d^2 <= a^2 b^2. The claim holds; the machine check was narrower than the wording.

latticectc.py:38-47: part (c) is headed 'n >= 2', but the Gram-matrix proof covers rank 2 only. The rank-n claim holds because a full-rank lattice in a subspace meets every non-empty open cone in that subspace. Re-derivation L7 checks rank 3. The claim holds; the heading is wider than the proof.

I could not refute STANDS. I re-read the sources myself through alphaXiv, and the quotes hold.

- HRR Sect. 2.2 (p.8) states and proves the invariant-time-function criterion by pull-back. The pull-back proof does not use the restriction to a single Killing generator.
- HRR Sect. 1.1 (p.4) describes BTZ as a quotient by two Killing vectors that "differ by a timelike vector".
- HRR p.19 adds that CTCs from a spacelike quotient appear "in the plane waves but not, for example, in flat space". This agrees with the rank-1 spatial case.
- GKLP 2208.09014v3 (PDF p.4, printed page 3): "A quick argument suggests that this cannot happen. In the covering space, image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones." Sect. 4 covers round-trip brane signals only, as the audit says.
- HRR Sect. 2.1 defines causal as "no closed non-spacelike curves", which is the notion the tree's (a) uses.

The mathematics also holds. A closed causal curve lifts to a causal curve from p to p+V with V in L. V cannot be 0, because Minkowski space has no closed causal curve. V lies in the closed convex cone. Conversely, a straight segment to p+V projects to a closed causal curve.

I checked the boundary claim with the general definition of stable causality, not only the eps-widening used in L8. A time function tau on the quotient lifts to an L-invariant tau on R^{1,2}. Take the lattice vectors V_m = (m, m, m*sqrt2+n) with delta_m = m*sqrt2+n tending to 0. Then tau(p+(m,m,0)) = tau(p-(0,0,delta_m)), which tends to tau(p). But tau strictly increases along the null line, so tau(p+(m,m,0)) >= tau(p+(1,1,0)) > tau(p). That is a contradiction, so the quotient is not stably causal, as latticectc.py:54-58 says.

1. REPRODUCIBILITY: the reported outcome did not reproduce. I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It printed 'REDERIVATION FAILED' and exited 1 (5m16s), not 'REDERIVATION OK, exit 0'. The one failing line is L5 'z3 unknowns: got 1 want 0', which is a 20 s solver timeout. I resolved it with v_l5unknown.py: 23 L5 cases return unknown at a 3 s timeout, and every one returns unsat at a 300 s timeout (2.5 to 23.9 s each). All 23 are spacelike closing vectors, so unsat (no chain) matches what L5 expects in each case. L5's substance survives: 0 mismatches in 720 cases, and 0 unknowns once the timeout is raised. The audit's '0 unknowns, exit 0' depends on the machine and the timeout; that is a discrepancy, not a refutation. The tree's own 'latticectc.py --selftest' returns SELFTEST OK.

2. ENCODING: what each check actually covers.
- L1 is a toy and tests nothing about the hypothesis. lift_loop never reads its gens argument (main passes [None]*n). It also works only in lattice coordinates, so it checks only that nearest-representative rounding tracks small steps. My vacuity guard V3: it passes with gens=['NOT A LATTICE']. So it cannot tell a discrete group from a non-discrete one. The audit already concedes this is a 'sanity check, not a proof'. Hatcher Prop. 1.30 is not checked here at all; it stays NAMED-NOT-READ, so the lifting step rests on topology, not on L1.
- L2, L3, L4 and L6 are genuine checks of the reduction lemma's ingredients, and they discriminate. V1: with the cone replaced by the non-convex spacelike region, L2 returns sat at spatial dims 1 and 2. V1b: with Cauchy-Schwarz dropped from the dimension-free route, it returns sat. V6: I added K = 3 legs with a symbolic V at spatial dim 1, and it returns unsat.
- L5 discriminates. V2: when legs may be causal in either time direction, there are 96 mismatches in 144 cases. But L5's 720 cases contain 0 null closing vectors, so it cannot test the null boundary (causal versus strictly timelike). V2c, my own check: null V = (1,1,0,0) and (5,3,4,0) do admit K = 2 chains, and the near-null spacelike V = (1,1,1/100,0) does not. So the boundary case holds, but L5 never tested it.
- L7's spacelike-span half is true by algebra: a positive-definite Gram matrix cannot fail the check. Only the timelike half has power: 60 of 60 found.
- L8 does not check the irrationality its conclusion rests on. V4: with s = 3/2 the sympy identity still gives residual 0 and the widened-metric check still passes. Yet (m,n) = (2,-3) gives the null lattice vector (2,2,0), so that quotient is not causal. The 'no causal lattice vector' half rests on sqrt2 being irrational, which is known but not computed here. The not-stably-causal half (eps = 1e-1 to 1e-6, exact) is sound.

Both of the audit's counterexamples fall outside the hypotheses of part (c), which requires A = |g1|^2 > 0 and C > 0 at rank 2. g1 = (1,1,0,0) is null, so A = 0. The generators (0,1,0,0) and (0,2,0,0) are Z-dependent, so the lattice is really rank 1. The finding survives in corrected form, and my V5 shows it inside (c)'s hypotheses. The audit's L9 should cite this lattice rather than its two out-of-hypothesis examples.

The checks that discriminate (L2/V1, L5/V2, L6, L7 timelike half, V6) confirm the reduction lemma, and no datum enters it. - that L8 does not compute the irrationality;

audits.published_statement: 0802.0658 Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'Since T_ab(x) defined at one point can be ill-behaved as it is generally divergent, one can question the soundness of these quantities. But as will be shown later, the noise kernel is finite for y != x. ... From this we see that all possible divergences for y != x will cancel. When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur. The above procedure will allow us to isolate the divergences and obtain a finite result.' p.25: N(x,y) 'is always finite for x != y (and off the light cone for massless theories)'. The review takes 'a more modest goal ... and leave[s] the discussion of point-wise limit to a later date'. Sec. 3.2 p.10: 'The noise kernel should be thought of as a distribution function, the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions.' The primary source, Phillips & Hu gr-qc/0010019, says on p.6 'Of course, without use of a regularized Green function, the y -> x limit is divergent', and on p.18 'The noise kernel ... diverges as the pair of points are brought together, representing the "standard" ultraviolet divergence'.
published_hypotheses: H1: a free (linear) scalar field with mass m and curvature coupling xi; stress tensor from Eqs. (5.9)/(5.10), p.27-28

H2: Wick's theorem for the 4-point function, 'for the case of free fields which we are considering' (p.30, Eq. 5.20), so the state is quasi-free (Gaussian). N is called the 'vacuum expectation value' of the bi-tensor (abstract; Phillips & Hu p.2)
H3: the physically acceptable states are Hadamard states (Sec. 3.1, p.8). The 'finite result' comes from modified point separation, which subtracts a Hadamard ansatz (Phillips & Hu Sec. IV)
H4: the pairs (x,x') and (y,y') each lie in a Riemann normal neighbourhood; for y -> x all four points lie in one (p.30)
H5: for massless theories, finiteness at x != y needs x and y off the light cone (p.25)
H6: the sentence 'divergences do occur' is asserted, not demonstrated. The review defers the pointwise limit (p.25) and computes no divergence coefficient
hypothesis_drift: No load-bearing hypothesis is dropped. noise.py:206-207 applies the sentence to the coincidence limit of the linear-field noise kernel. The file keeps H1 elsewhere: noise.py:202 says 'for a linear field', and noise.py:222-224 excludes nonminimal coupling and interacting fields ('H1 is essential').

A paraphrase, not a drift (noise.py:206): the tree says the Sec. 3.2 quote 'is about SEPARATED points'. Sec. 3.2 never says 'separated points'. It says the counterterms cancel and then qualifies: 'the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions' (p.10). The paraphrase agrees with that qualification and with p.25 ('finite for x != y').

Omitted context (noise.py:206-207): the tree does not carry the source's next sentence, 'The above procedure will allow us to isolate the divergences and obtain a finite result'. That finite coincident result comes from Hadamard subtraction (Phillips & Hu Sec. IV, Eq. 4.10), which regularises the pointwise kernel. Leaving it out does not tilt the tree's case: it supports the tree's narrowing. The tree's own finiteness route, worldline smearing (Fewster Sec. 3.3), is a different argument and stays NAMED (noise.py:207-211, 275).
Not carried, and harmless: H4 and H5. Both concern finiteness at separated points, not the coincidence divergence the tree cites.

audits.name: Quantum state teleportation protocol (Bennett-Brassard-Crepeau-Jozsa-Peres-Wootters 1993)

source.located: C.H. Bennett, G. Brassard, C. Crepeau, R. Jozsa, A. Peres, W.K. Wootters, 'Teleporting an unknown quantum state via dual classical and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen channels', Phys. Rev. A and the Fig. 1 caption); (ii) Bennett, Brassard, Popescu, Schumacher, Smolin and Wootters, arXiv:quant-ph/9511027, p.1, whose authors include Bennett, Brassard and Wootters from the 1993 paper, restating it, and p.4 on LOCC monotonicity; (iii) Boschi et al., arXiv:quant-ph/9710013, pp.1-2, which quotes the 1993 abstract.
