source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1505.07831, quant-ph/9511027 and quant-ph/9710013, with page text returned verbatim. Experimental confirmation read in 1707.00934.

audits.published_statement: As restated in 1505.07831, pp.1-2: 'an unknown quantum state of a physical system is measured and subsequently reconstructed or reassembled at a remote location (the physical constituents of the original system remain at the sending location). This process requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication. Most importantly, it requires the resource of quantum entanglement.' The protocol: Alice and Bob 'share two qubits, A and B, prepared in a pure entangled state. In the ideal case, this is taken to be maximally entangled ... Alice is given another qubit a whose state rho is unknown ... Bell detection, which projects her qubits a and A into one of the four Bell states (P_k x I)|Phi> ... Bob's qubit B is simultaneously projected onto P_k^dag rho P_k ... Alice communicates the classical outcome k ... Bob applies P_k to recover the original input state rho', with F = 1 in the ideal case. 'Alice's input state is assumed to be unknown, otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation.' For finite d: 'Pauli operators P_k replaced by U_k and the classical channel involves distinguishing d^2 signals.' quant-ph/9511027, p.1: 'an arbitrary unknown qubit can be faithfully transmitted via a pair of maximally-entangled qubits (e.g. two spin-1/2 particles in a pure singlet state) previously shared between sender and receiver, and a 2-bit classical message'.
published_hypotheses: P1: the state is UNKNOWN to the sender (1505.07831 p.2; quant-ph/9511027 p.1). For a known state the task reduces to remote state preparation.
P2: a maximally entangled pure pair is PREVIOUSLY SHARED between sender and receiver. The original used a singlet (per quant-ph/9511027 p.1); any Bell pair is equivalent (1505.07831 p.1).
P3: a complete, ideal Bell measurement that distinguishes all four Bell states (1505.07831 p.2, and p.4 requirement (3)).
P4: a classical channel carries the 2-bit outcome (log2 d^2 bits for a d-level system) to the receiver, who applies the conditional unitary.
P5: ideal, noiseless operations give fidelity 1. With noise the fidelity is below 1 and purification is needed (quant-ph/9511027).
P6: standard linear quantum mechanics with the Born rule. It is implicit in all three restatements and stated in none. 'Excludes superluminal communication' is a theorem inside it.
P7: finite-dimensional systems. The original treats a qubit; the source's own generalisation covers any finite d.
hypothesis_drift: RESOURCE STATE (harmless): transit.py:91-95 uses |Phi+> with corrections [I, X, Z, ZX] in the Bell order [Phi+, Psi+, Phi-, Psi-]. The original used the singlet |Psi-> (quant-ph/9511027 p.1). The two differ by a local unitary, and rederive C1 and C2 show both return psi exactly on all four outcomes. Not a narrowing.

IDEALITY (named, consistent): the tree's hypotheses 'ideal noiseless Bell pair' and 'ideal Bell-basis measurement' (transit.py:91-95) match P2, P3 and P5. The prose at transit.py:20-22, 192-195 and 280 says EXACT/PERFECT without the word 'ideal', and TRANSIT_IS_EXACT = True (transit.py:150) holds only under P3/P5. Through a Werner resource of singlet fraction F the fidelity is (2F+1)/3 (C6). Measured fidelities are 0.831 +- 0.009 (quant-ph/9710013 p.8), >= 0.83 at 143 km (1505.07831 Fig.2) and 0.80 +- 0.01 at up to 1400 km (1707.00934).

UNKNOWN STATE (consistent): H_tele (specthm.py:1188, 1206) carries P1. specthm.py:1212 says a KNOWN state can be re-prepared rather than teleported, which matches 1505.07831 p.2 on remote state preparation. No drift.

SCALE (covered by the source): the tree applies the result to the reconstruction specification (ledger.py:1357-1372, specthm.py:1170-1222), an object's state, while transit.py runs d = 2 only. The source's own finite-d generalisation (1505.07831 p.2) covers this: d^2 outcomes, 2 log2 d classical bits and log2 d ebits (C7, checked numerically at d = 3). CLASSICAL_BITS_PER_QUBIT = 2 (transit.py:140) is correctly per qubit. No drift.

ADDED, OVERSTATED (tree prose): 'NO WORLDLINE CROSSES ANYTHING' (transit.py:21-22, 192-195). The source says only that the physical constituents of the original system stay at the sending location (1505.07831 p.1) and that classical communication is required. Bob's half of the pair and the two classical bits do cross the distance at <= c. transit.py says so itself at lines 46-50 and 251-256 and records TRAVERSAL_IS_REMOVED = False at line 154. This is an internal inconsistency in the tree's wording, and the constant is the correct statement. A discrepancy, not a refutation.

ADDED, MIS-NAMED (tree prose): 'CONSERVATION LAW' (transit.py:24, 213, 221, 283). The fall in Alice|Bob entanglement from 1 ebit to 0 is computed true here (C4: the state after measurement is a product). The principle at work is LOCC non-increase of entanglement (quant-ph/9511027 p.4), not conservation: after the measurement Alice's own two qubits hold one ebit locally. The conclusion 'one pair, one transit' stands; only the name is imprecise.

ASSERTED, NOT COMPUTED (tree code): CHANNEL_BITS_AFTER = 0.0 (transit.py:139) and A's S = 1 bit (transit.py:230, 342, from entropy2 of a hard-coded I/2) are constants in transit.py, not computed from the state after measurement. Computed here (C4), both are true.

ADVANTAGE BY CONSTRUCTION (tree code): advantage_over_light(D) = arrival_time(D) - D/c, with arrival_time(D) = D/c (transit.py:145-146), so it is identically 0 (C9). The word 'provably' (transit.py:44, 249) is earned by the no-signalling computation (C3, C5, C8, and transit.py's own section 3) together with an assumption the tree leaves unnamed: classical signals travel at <= c (special relativity). A real channel arrives no earlier than D/c, so the true advantage is <= 0.
COUNT WORDING: 'twelve trials' (transit.py:21, 280) means 3 trials x 4 outcomes in report(). The selftest runs 5 x 4 = 20. Wording discrepancy only.
UNNAMED IN BOTH: P6 (linear QM with the Born rule). The tree's 'provably' holds within it. Under nonlinear modifications of QM, entanglement can signal (Gisin 1990, Polchinski 1991; NAMED-NOT-READ).
ATTRIBUTION: transit.py names the mechanism (lines 10-13, 276) but cites no paper for it.

audits.lacked_data: The result is a finite-dimensional theorem of linear quantum mechanics and uses no measured input, so no moved datum can shift it. What the 1993 authors lacked was any experiment. The experiments that followed (Boschi 1997: 0.831; Ma 2012: >= 0.83 at 143 km; Ren 2017: 0.80 at up to 1400 km) confirm it at the fidelities noise models predict, (2F+1)/3 (C6). None shows signalling, and each needed the entangled half distributed in advance, which is the tree's own point that the corridor must be traversed. Only a failure of P6 (linear QM with the Born rule) could overturn the no-signalling part. The tree does not name P6, and nothing checked here tests it. The papers showing nonlinear-QM signalling (Gisin 1990, Polchinski 1991) are NAMED-NOT-READ. As far as can be checked here, M's hypothesis that earlier physicists lacked data does not change this result: the later data confirms it and does not contradict it.
audits.grade_evidence:
The tree uses the result under the source's hypotheses: an unknown state, an ideal Bell pair, an ideal Bell measurement and 2 classical bits per qubit. These match the restatements (1505.07831 pp.1-2; quant-ph/9511027 p.1). A symbolic re-derivation for a general state confirms every point the tree relies on (C1-C8). No datum enters, and later experiments confirm the protocol. verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the NARROWED grade in either direction. It holds, but the audit has several factual slips that need correcting. R&G 2003 is not on arXiv, so I could not read the chapter myself either. What I could do was read Johnson & Goldblatt 2015 (arXiv:1505.03813v1) at source through alphaXiv; the audit had marked it NAMED-NOT-READ.

(1) The audit misquotes J&G. Their Table 9 (p.25) gives upper-crust N as 150 ± 12 ppm (standard error of the mean), not '150 +/- 22'. Lower crust is 17 ± 6 ppm and the total crust average is 120 ± 9 ppm, for 1.7 ± 0.1 × 10^18 kg N. The 120 ppm total is the figure to compare against R&G's 56 ppm bulk; setting the 150 ppm upper value against bulk compares unlike quantities. At 120 ppm, N still binds, with a factor of 214.0, and crust/chondrite is 20.0x. The audit's conclusion survives: the binding element and the ranking do not change.

(2) J&G Table 1 (p.4) lists the R&G (2003, 2014) continental-crust N mass as 1.1 × 10^18 kg. 56 ppm × 1.9 × 10^22 kg (J&G's crust mass, Table 7) gives 1.06 × 10^18 kg. That is independent corroboration that pyrolite's mislabelled 'Na, 56, ppm' row really is N = 56 ppm. J&G also write (p.26) that the R&G value is lower because it rests on older compilations (Wedepohl 1995, Wlotzka 1972). So 'a datum moved' is now READ, not presumed.

(3) The carbon hypothesis bites harder at J&G's values. N binds only while crust C exceeds 8.889 × crust N. That is 498 ppm at 56 ppm N, 1067 ppm at J&G's 120 ppm total, and 1333 ppm at their 150 ppm upper. The tree's C value (2000 / 1990 ppm) has no R&G provenance and no source read here. So 'the crust binds on N' depends on crustal C, a datum from outside this result. The audit already records that as a condition. The destination ranking does not depend on it: with the tree's C, the crust factor is at least 114.1 whatever N is, so the chondrite wins by at least 10.7x. That is why DATA-DEPENDENT is not warranted for the conclusions that matter.

(4) The audit overstates in a few small places, none of which moves the grade:
- It says pyrolite has 'one visible transcription fault'. There is a second: the UCC 2003 file has S 62 ppm where the 2014 file has 621 ppm.
- It says the 'unc_2sigma column is empty'. That is true of BCC only; UCC 2003 carries 2-sigma values.
- Its counts of entries that '=BCC/=UCC' use a 3 % tolerance, not exact equality (Sc 21.4 vs 21.9, Co 17.5 vs 17.3, As 4.7 vs 4.8).

(5) I checked the audit's arithmetic and it is right:
- N binds at 458.6 with bulk values and 309.4 with upper.
- The C threshold is 498 ppm.

The bulk-to-bulk comparison is J&G's total, and that total is internally inconsistent in v1. 0.53x150 + 0.47x17 = 87.5 ppm, and 1.7e18 kg over their 1.9e22 kg crust mass (Table 7) = 89.5 ppm. Neither gives the printed 120. This is recorded as a discrepancy in the preprint, not a refutation; the journal version was not read. The bulk J&G range is therefore 88-120 ppm:
- N factor 293.5 at 87.5 ppm and 214.0 at 120 ppm;

At 150 ppm the audit's 171.2 and 16.0 are reproduced. In every case N still binds, because the stated stop-binding limit is 225 ppm, set by the tree's own C. The qualitative moves_conclusion follows.

(2) J&G Table 1 lists R&G (2003, 2014) continental-crust N as 1.1x10^18 kg, which is 57.9 ppm over 1.9e22 kg. That independently backs reading the restatement's mislabelled 'Na 56' row as N = 56 ppm.

Their new compilation (e.g. 261 shale and 247 granite samples) raises crustal N about 1.6-2.1x. So the 2003 figure did lack data. R1: F_S(0) = -b_0, and b_0 = 0 iff alpha~^S_1 = 0, so gamma = 0 is a root exactly then.
R2: F_S'(0) kappa (1-6xi)^2 = 12 + kappa m^2/(24 pi^2) > 0. At alpha~^S_1 = 0, gamma = 0 is therefore a SIMPLE zero, and by the implicit function theorem no second real zero branches off from it.
R3 (z3, with a vacuity guard and a control): at alpha~^S_1 = 0 and b_2 >= 0, F_S < 0 on the WHOLE real growing side gamma < 0, since J > 0 there. So there is no real growing zero at all. With b_2 < 0 a zero is admissible (sat). This matches the tree's S bracket firing at b_2 = -1e100 and not at +1e100.
R4: alpha~^S_1 > 0 implies F_S(0) > 0.
R5: F_TT(0) = 0 identically; F_TT'(0) = m^2/(6 pi^2) - 60/kappa; a_TT = 4m^2.

The audit graded OPEN for one reason: it could not read the source. I read it through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2604.01047v1, and the quota did not trip. With the text in hand, OPEN no longer holds, and the evidence supports NARROWED.

READ at source:

In the source that interval is the hypothesis of the BOUNDED/DECAY clause, and Z is taken in the w^2 variable of Q. The auditor's 'unnamed variable' alternative ("taken in w^2 the same interval would be the oscillating side") is the source's own convention.

I confirmed with sympy, in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/refute/thm416_variable_map.py, that F_S(γ) = −Q(−γ). audits.lacked_data: In 1996 the authors lacked the Higgs mass (measured 2012), a precise m_W (about +/- 0.1 GeV then, about 0.01 GeV now) and the post-LEP-II electroweak fits. EVIDENCE THAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE THE CONCLUSION, all COMPUTED here: (a) The leading exponent 8 pi^2/g^2 is a property of the self-dual BPST solution. By the Bogomolny bound it is also a lower bound on the Euclidean action of every Q = 1 gauge-Higgs path. It contains neither m_H nor m_t, so the missing Higgs mass cannot lift the suppression; through the constrained-instanton term it can only deepen it. (b) The move in m_W from 1996 to 2026 shifts the exponent by less than 0.1 decade. (c) The authors' 1/29 against today's 1/29.49 (tree inputs) is 2.68 decades, and the whole convention band is about 15 decades, against a suppression of about 160 decades. EVIDENCE THE OTHER WAY: none found for the T = 0 exponent. Data genuinely matter for the prefactor (m_H-dependent, not read by the tree) and for the high-energy collider rate, which the tree already holds CONTESTED in S11. On the computable legs, M's hypothesis is therefore not supported for this result. The source itself could not be read in this stage, so that verdict rests on the tree's captures plus the re-derivation, not on the page.

All five alphaXiv calls hit the quota, and arxiv.org, alphaxiv.org, export.arxiv.org and inspirehep are blocked by the egress proxy. M's rule forbids flattening an unread source to STANDS. Everything that WAS computed points one way, and it is recorded so the next reader need not redo it. (1) The form exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) = exp(-2 S_inst), with S_inst = 8 pi^2/g^2, is machine-checked from the BPST solution (19/19 PASS). (2) The Bogomolny bound shows every Q = 1 path in the Higgs phase is at least this suppressed. (3) The tree's figures (1/alpha_W = 29.49, 10^-160.95, 10^189.10) reproduce independently. (4) Eq. (2.8) pairs 10^-170 with 1/29, an internal discrepancy of 11.73 decades that the tree already records and does not repair. 10^-170 matches a different convention for alpha (1/alpha_W = 31.15), so this is a misprint-class discrepancy, not a refutation. (5) No moved datum moves the conclusion. The tree's use carries one unnamed hypothesis: the scheme and scale of alpha_W at leading order, about 12 decades of convention inside 10^-160.95 and 10^189.10 (massform.py:527-533). It is immaterial to every refusal that rests on it (S11, SR5). Of the five conventions computed, the tree's gives the second-weakest suppression; only the source's own 1/29 is weaker, by 2.68 decades. None moves the exponent away from about 10^-160. If a read of the source confirms the captures, the computed legs would support STANDS with that hypothesis named. verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE: read hep-ph/9603208 at source and test whether the OPEN still holds
verifiers.reason:
The audit graded OPEN for one reason only: the source could not be read in its stage, because of the alphaXiv quota and proxy blocks. That reason no longer holds. I read the paper at source with alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-ph/9603208v2, and it confirms every capture the tree uses, verbatim and at the stated page.

What the source shows:
(a) PDF p.6 (printed p.5) carries the T=0 sentence word for word: 'At zero energies and temperatures, the transition between vacua with different n[omega] is a tunnelling event which is described by instantons [22] (constrained instantons in theories with the Higgs mechanism [47]). In pure Yang-Mills theory an instanton is the solution to the Euclidean field equations...'
(b) PDF p.7 (printed p.6) prints 'S_inst = 8 pi^2/g^2' and eq. (2.7), 'the tunnelling amplitude is proportional to A_inst ∝ e^{-S_inst}'. Eq. (2.8) follows verbatim: 'In the electroweak theory, the tunneling probability is unobservably small, Gamma_inst ∝ exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) ~ 10^-170, where alpha_W = g^2/4pi = alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29'. The probability is therefore the squared amplitude, exp(-2 S_inst). The audit listed that leg as 'NOT checkable here'; it is now READ.
(c) H4, the qualifier the audit says the tree dropped, is settled by the source itself, in the direction the audit computed. On the same page, eq. (2.9) gives the constrained-instanton weight as exp(-8pi^2/g^2 - pi^2 rho^2 v^2), and the source states: 'Clearly, the tunnelling rate is still suppressed by the exponential factor (2.8).' So the exponent applies to the Higgs theory on the source's own authority, not only through the auditor's Bogomolny argument.
(d) Sec. 4.1 on PDF p.12 (printed p.11) is verbatim. So are eqs. (2.2)-(2.5) on printed pp.4-5, including 'the factor 1/3 comes from the baryon number of a quark, while the factor 3·3 is due to colour and number of generations'.
(e) The internal discrepancy in eq. (2.8) is real and was correctly recorded. My own arithmetic gives 10^-158.268 for 1/29, against the printed 10^-170, a gap of 11.73 decades; 10^-170 corresponds to 1/alpha_W = 31.15. That is a misprint-class discrepancy: it is no refutation, and nothing should be repaired.
(f) The tree's figures reproduce independently: v = 246.2196 and 1/alpha_W = 29.4913 give 10^-160.949. The audit's rederive script still returns 19/19 PASS.

Later literature. One discover_papers pass returned no title that revises the T=0 leading exponent. The titles were on prefactors, the high-energy collider suppression, the valley versus constrained instanton, and a non-zero Weinberg angle. Those are titles only and I did not read them. Even so, the Bogomolny bound and the source's own eq. (2.9) mean any Higgs or size effect can only deepen the suppression.

The tree's use stays inside the source's regime: T = 0, zero energy, the exponent only, and 'NO RATE IS PRINTED' because no prefactor was read. That meets the audit's own stated route to STANDS.

The unnamed hypothesis remains: the scheme and scale of alpha_W at leading order. Taking the audit's computed band, of which only the source's own 1/29 is read, it spans about 12 decades of the roughly 161 inside 10^-160.95 and 10^189.10 (massform.py:527-533). It should be named, H-SCHEME, beside 'no prefactor read'. It is immaterial to S11 and SR5 and does not narrow the class of use.

Two smaller points:
- The tree's RS96-T0 quote stops before the source's '(constrained instantons in theories with the Higgs mechanism [47])' parenthetical. This omission favours nothing: the source's next paragraph upholds the exponent in the Higgs theory.
- The 't Hooft PRL 37 (1976) 8 classic is still NAMED-NOT-READ. The grade here rests on the review, which is read.

Grade: STANDS, with H-SCHEME named. It is not OPEN, since the source is now READ. It is not NARROWED, because the source states no validity condition that the tree's per-transition use goes beyond. verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script, check its encoding against the published statement, run the vacuity guard
verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN. I copied the audit script to verify/rederive/rs96_copy.py and ran it: 19/19 PASS, exit 0, with every printed figure identical to the audit's. Those figures are 1/alpha_W = 29.4913, 10^-160.9489, 10^189.0961, 1/29 giving 10^-158.2677, a gap of 11.73 decades, 31.15 for 10^-170, a convention spread of 14.89 decades, and 0.0533 decades for 1 sigma in m_W.

ENCODING. The core check is the real theorem, not a toy of it. The script builds the BPST field from 't Hooft symbols, computes F^a with structure constants eps^{abc}, and verifies F^aF^a = 192 rho^4/(x^2+rho^2)^4 exactly. It then checks self-duality and gets S = 8 pi^2/g^2 and |Q| = 1 by exact integration. The generic-F Bogomolny identity is also a genuine identity.

The script has three weak spots:
(i) Checks (1a) to (1c) are tautological algebra: they define S_inst and then rearrange it.
(ii) The action integral uses the hard-coded 192 rho^4 form, not the computed FF. In the amp=1 mutation below, the S check still PASSED while the FF check failed, so the coupling between the two is only implicit.
(iii) Two things were assumed and never checked: that the g in the action is the g in m_W = g v/2, and that probability = exp(-2S).

I closed all three in verify/rederive/supplement.py, 5/5 PASS:
- |D Phi0|^2 = (1/2)(g v/2)^2 W^a W^a for D = d - i g (sigma^a/2) W^a, so the tree's g = 2 m_W/v is the action's g.
- F^aF^a computed directly is O(4)-radial in four directions, and integrating it gives 8 pi^2/g^2.
- |e^{-S}|^2 = exp(-4 pi/alpha_W).
- The source's eq. (2.9) exponent, -8 pi^2/g^2 - pi^2 v^2 rho^2, is bounded above by -8 pi^2/g^2, approached as rho -> 0.

VACUITY. Every check fails when its hypothesis is negated:
- Structure constant doubled: the FF and self-duality checks FAIL.
- Ansatz amplitude 1 instead of 2: FF and self-duality FAIL, but the hard-coded S check still passes (weak spot (ii) above).
- Normalisation 1/2g^2: the S check FAILS.
- Dual taken without the 1/2: both Bogomolny identities FAIL.
- exp(-S) in place of exp(-2S): FAIL.
- 1/alpha_W = 10 added to the scheme list: the 'below 10^-150' check FAILS.
- Supplement, Higgs generator sigma instead of sigma/2: the m_W check FAILS.
- Supplement, amplitude 1: the action diverges and the check FAILS.
- Supplement, flipping the sign of the (2.9) Higgs term: FAILS.

SOURCE NOW READ. This changes the grade basis. The audit's OPEN rested only on the unread page. This time alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-ph/9603208v2 succeeded and returned the PDF text. Every tree capture is verbatim and correctly located:
- RS96-anom, eqs (2.2)-(2.4): printed p.4 (PDF p.5).
- RS96-T0: printed p.5 (PDF p.6).
- RS96-2.8: printed p.6 (PDF p.7). The page reads 'Gamma_inst ∝ exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) ~ 10^-170, where alpha_W = g^2/4 pi = alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29'.
- RS96-inst: Sec. 4.1, printed p.11 (PDF p.12).

The page also prints 'S_inst = 8 pi^2/g^2 and the tunnelling amplitude is proportional to A_inst ∝ e^{-S_inst} (2.7)', and m_W = g v/2. That settles the audit's 'NOT checkable: exp(-2S)': probability = |amplitude|^2 = exp(-16 pi^2/g^2), the source's own construction.

On H4: the tree's T=0 quote ends at 'instantons'. The source sentence continues '(constrained instantons in theories with the Higgs mechanism [47])', and p.6 states 'Clearly, the tunnelling rate is still suppressed by the exponential factor (2.8)'. The dropped qualifier is therefore harmless in direction at source, matching the audit's Bogomolny argument.

The 10^-170 at 1/29 discrepancy (11.73 decades) is confirmed at source. It is a misprint-class discrepancy, recorded and not repaired, not a refutation.

LATER LITERATURE. One discover_papers call returned two candidates, neither read here:
- 2508.21825, zero-T baryon-number violation from Higgs bubble collisions. This is a non-vacuum initial state, outside the source's H1 'zero energies and temperatures'.
- 2011.07167, a high-energy collision suppression paper.

Neither, as summarised, alters the vacuum T=0 leading exponent.

GRADE. With the page read and the re-derivation non-vacuous, the evidence supports STANDS, with two named hypotheses the tree should carry: H-SCHEME (the alpha_W convention at leading order, about 12 decades inside 10^-160.95 and 10^189.10) and 'no prefactor read'. The audit's own OPEN was correct for its stage. It is superseded by this read, not refuted. Its own '-> STANDS' condition is met except that the discovery pass was thin: one query, results unread.

This stage read the source, which the audit could not. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-ph/9603208v2 worked, and get_paper_content returned the full text (244k characters, saved to tool-results). The page and number checks below are READ.

(1) The tree's captures are verbatim and correctly located.
- RS96-anom: eqs (2.2)-(2.5), printed p.4/5.
- RS96-T0: printed p.5. The source continues: "(constrained instantons in theories with the Higgs mechanism [47]). In pure Yang-Mills theory an instanton is ... an absolute minimum of the Euclidean action in the sector N[A]=1".
- RS96-2.8: printed p.6, "Gamma_inst ∝ exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) ~ 10^-170, where alpha_W = g^2/4pi = alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29". The source's first relation is ∝; the tree transcribes it as '~'. This is a trivial transcription difference.
- RS96-inst: Sec. 4.1, printed p.11.

(2) Two legs the audit marked not checkable are READ at source.
- Eq. (2.7) gives amplitude ∝ e^{-S_inst} with S_inst = 8 pi^2/g^2. Eq. (2.8) is the probability, so exp(-2S) is the source's own definition.
- Eq. (2.9) gives exp(-8pi^2/g^2 - pi^2 v^2 rho^2), and p.6 says "Clearly, the tunnelling rate is still suppressed by the exponential factor (2.8)". The Higgs-phase/Bogomolny direction is therefore the source's own statement, not only a computation.

(3) Data rows.
- value_then 1/29: confirmed READ.
- sin^2 theta_W = 0.23: READ, printed p.8 ("For the actual value sin^2 theta_W = 0.23").
- m_H unknown: READ, printed p.7 ("in the MSM the only grossly unknown parameter is the mass of the Higgs boson").
- m_t = 175 GeV: READ, Sec. 5.6, as the value the paper uses.
- The paper prints no m_W value that enters the exponent. It uses 1/29 directly, so the m_W 'value_then ~80.3' row is context only, as the audit says.
- value_now: 1/alpha_W = 29.4913 and 10^-160.9489 re-computed independently. The recalled scheme values (29.59, 30.59, 31.73) agree with my own recall of PDG inputs. They stay RECALLED.
- 5.4575 decades per unit of 1/alpha_W equals 4pi/ln10; correct.
- 1-sigma m_W shift of 0.053 decades: correct.
- Derived 10^189.0961 = 28.1472 + 160.9489: correct.
- The rederive script runs 19/19 PASS.

(4) One wrong number in lacked_data. Clause (b) says "the move in m_W from 1996 to 2026 shifts the exponent by less than 0.1 decade". With the audit's own value_then of 80.3 GeV the shift is 0.249 decades; with a recalled PDG-1996 value of 80.33 it is 0.128. Both exceed 0.1. The rederive script's '<0.1 decade' PASS tests only the 1-sigma move, not the 1996->2026 move. This is a misstatement of size, not of direction. It is immaterial against about 160 decades, and moves_conclusion = No still follows. It should be corrected to about 0.1-0.25 decade.

(5) M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not presumed. The leading exponent contains no m_H and no m_t (eq. (2.9) READ), and every data move is a few decades at most against about 160. M's hypothesis is not supported for this result.

(6) The grade. OPEN rested only on the unread source and the undiscovered later literature. The source is now read and confirms every capture. One discover_papers pass returned only abstracts, which were not read: 2406.05180, 2011.07167, 1809.10833, hep-ph/9306208, hep-th/9512064, hep-ph/9501253 and 2608.04595. These concern the prefactor, vacuum stability, the collider rate and constrained/valley instantons. None of the abstracts claims to change the T=0 leading exponent. That meets the audit's own '-> STANDS' condition, with two caveats: the later literature is screened at abstract level only, and H-SCHEME (the alpha_W convention at leading order, about 12-15 decades) must be named beside 'no prefactor read'. The eq. (2.8) 10^-170 vs 1/29 discrepancy (11.73 decades) stays RECORDED, NOT REPAIRED.

audits.name: FLAG Review 2024 nucleon sigma terms (sigma_piN, sigma_s) and their interpretation

source.located: FLAG Review 2024, Y. Aoki et al. (Flavour Lattice Averaging Group), arXiv:2411.04268v3, Sec. 10.4.4, Eqs. (431)-(433), (446)-(450), pp.260-275. The journal reference Phys. Rev. D 113, 014508 (2026) is as restated in audits/sigma-term-scan.json; it was not read here.
source.via: This stage did not open the PDF itself. Every alphaXiv call returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded': answer_pdf_queries twice, get_paper_content once and discover_papers once. The egress proxy blocks arxiv.org, www.alphaxiv.org and flag.unibe.ch (403). The statement is taken from two independent transcriptions of the same pages. (i) The sibling DOCKET 67 audit audits/sigma-term-scan.json READ 2411.04268 at source through alphaXiv (pp.11, 260-275) earlier in this run. It quotes Eqs.(447)-(450), the p.273 sentence on the 2.7 sigma difference, the p.274 sentence 'around three standard deviations', the definition sigma_q = m_q dM_N/dm_q (Eqs.431-433 and 446), the neutral-pion isospin limit, the caveats 'remains an issue' and 'the averages may change', and how sigma_s(2+1+1) was built (MILC 12C times the FLAG m_s). (ii) The tree holds its own quotes at massform.py:1314-1350. The two agree on every number and every sentence they both quote. A third restatement of the averages, in 2506.23902, is recorded by audits/qcd-trace-anomaly-nucleon-mass.json and was not read here.

audits.published_statement: From FLAG 2024 Sec.10.4.4, as transcribed by the sibling audit's at-source read and by massform.py:1314-1350. Eq.(447): 'N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 : sigma_piN = 60.9(6.5) MeV'. Eq.(448): 'N_f = 2 + 1 : sigma_piN = 42.2(2.4) MeV'. Eq.(449): 'N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 : sigma_s = 41.0(8.8) MeV'. Eq.(450): 'N_f = 2 + 1 : sigma_s = 44.9(6.4) MeV'. p.273: 'there is now a 2.7 sigma difference between the N_f = 2 + 1 and N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 FLAG averages. This is unlikely to be due to the inclusion of charm quarks in the sea. The control of excited-state contributions remains an issue ... If this constraint is relaxed then a sigma term of around 42 MeV is obtained.' p.274: 'The N_f = 2 + 1 + 1 lattice average is in agreement with Hoferichter et al. [1035] ... while there is some tension, at the level of around three standard deviations, with the lattice average for N_f = 2 + 1.' p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses.' The definition is sigma_q = m_q <N|qbar q|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q (Feynman-Hellmann). On the charm term, p.275 gives sigma_c = 107(22) MeV from ETM 19.
published_hypotheses: sigma_q = m_q dM_N/dm_q is a first derivative (Feynman-Hellmann), taken at the physical point with the QCD coupling and scale held fixed (Eqs.431-433 and 446).

The isospin-symmetric limit is defined with the neutral pion (about 135 MeV). The Roy-Steiner value 59.1(3.5) MeV is in the charged-pion convention, and converting between the two shifts sigma_piN by 3.1(5) MeV.
The averages use only results that pass the FLAG quality criteria. The N_f = 2+1 error was inflated by about 10% because chi^2/dof = 1.23.
sigma_s(2+1+1) comes from a single study: MILC 12C's <N|ss|N> multiplied by the FLAG m_s average.
Control of excited states (N pi, N pi pi) 'remains an issue' and 'the averages may change'. FLAG does not attribute the 2.7 sigma split to charm in the sea.
'Shift in M_N due to nonzero quark masses' is the first-order reading of sigma. FLAG does not claim that sigma equals the finite difference M_N - M_N(m_q = 0).

audits.name: Gravitational binding of order G M/(R c^2) negligible at payload scale

source.located: There is no single paper behind this. The external content is Newton's law of gravitation and the Newtonian self-energy of a bound body, U = -k G M^2/R (k = 3/5 for a uniform ball; k = 3/(5-n) for a polytrope, from Chandrasekhar 1939, 'An Introduction to the Study of Stellar Structure', ch. IV), plus the value of G from CODATA. The CODATA 2022 paper is arXiv:2409.03787 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga).
source.via: All three alphaXiv tools (answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content, discover_papers) returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded' this session. The egress proxy refuses arxiv.org (curl CONNECT 403; WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED). So the self-energy formula was not read at any source. It was RE-DERIVED here from Newton's law: sympy gives k = 3/5 and k = 3/4 exactly, and Lane-Emden numerics for n = 1.5 and n = 3 agree with 3/(5-n) to within 5e-3. The value of G was READ from the CODATA 2022 table shipped in scipy 1.17.1 (scipy.constants._codata, _current_codata = 'CODATA 2022'): G = 6.67430e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, u = 1.5e-15. That table is a machine copy of the NIST values, not the CODATA paper itself.

audits.published_statement: Textbook and Chandrasekhar form, restated here, NOT read at source, and re-derived: a self-gravitating body of mass M and radius R has gravitational potential energy U = -k G M^2/R, with k = 3/5 for uniform density and k = 3/(5-n) for a polytrope of index n < 5. Hence |U|/(M c^2) = k G M/(R c^2). The tree uses only the order-of-magnitude form G M/(R c^2) and leaves out k ('No shape factor is claimed', massform.py:2093).
published_hypotheses: HN1 Newtonian (weak-field) gravity. It holds when G M/(R c^2) << 1, and post-Newtonian corrections are O((G M/R c^2)^2).

HN2 A single self-gravitating body with a definite mass distribution. k depends on the density profile: 3/5 uniform, 3/4 for n=1, 6/7 for n=1.5, 3/2 for n=3, and it diverges as n -> 5 or as the mass concentrates to a point.
HN3 G = 6.67430(15)e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2. CODATA 2018 and CODATA 2022 give the same value.
HN4 R is the physical radius of the body, i.e. the scale over which its mass is spread.
hypothesis_drift: SUBSTITUTED R (weakens HN4). The R used is R_BEKENSTEIN_M = 1.0 m, the radius H-R sets for the Bekenstein comparison (massform.py:2010 and 2094; H-R is defined at massform.py:830-831). It is not the physical size of a 70 kg body. At water density a 70 kg body is a ball of radius 0.256 m, giving |U|/Mc^2 = 1.22e-25 (2.35 times the tree's figure), or a cylinder 1.75 m tall and 0.113 m in radius, giving 8.2e-26 (1.57 times, by Monte Carlo). The worst case under a density cap, a ball at osmium density, gives 3.45e-25 (6.6 times). So the printed 5.2e-26 under-states the realistic ratio by a factor of 1.6 to 6.6. The order of magnitude holds and 'negligible' is unaffected. This is recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation.
k DROPPED, and the tree says so openly: 'No shape factor is claimed' (massform.py:2093) and 'of order' (massform.py:494). That is honest as written, and the tree does not claim an exact figure.

The SCOPE qualifier carries weight and is present: 'negligible at payload scale' (massform.py:496; H-AME at massform.py:827-829; D28 at massform.py:2880-2881). The same ratio is 2.1e-6 for the Sun and 0.17 for a 1.4 Msun neutron star of radius 12 km. At that compactness gravitational binding does make matter lighter per baryon than 56Fe, so H-AME is false beyond payload scale, and the tree does not use it there. No drift.

H-AME's literal wording, 'no bound state carries baryon number more cheaply' (massform.py:493), is false on its own for every self-gravitating lump, which is lighter per baryon by |U|/B. The tree names the exception in the same sentence ('Gravitational binding could, but ...', massform.py:494) and folds it into H-AME at massform.py:827-829. It is named, not dropped.

NOT ADDRESSED, a hypothesis the tree does not state: the mutual gravitational binding between the payload and the B units of antibaryon number that are 'held apart' at separation d. It is of order G M^2/d, so at most 5.2e-26 Mc^2 for d >= 1 m. It grows without bound as d -> 0, but then the antimatter is not held apart. This is not drift in the claim as worded; it is a gap in scope.

verifiers.reason:
1. RE-RUN. A copy of the script at verify/rederive/2309.05759-eqs76-77.py gives 14/14 PASS and exit 0. The figures reproduce: 6.372236e-64, 42.196 orders, a 1e-10 match to branelink.sme_coefficient(), and 3.08e-26 m.

2. ENCODING AND VACUITY. The script checks the tree's arithmetic, not the theorem. Its checks are the tensor factor 3beta^2/4, zeta(3), the tree's number re-typed from CODATA, and d/dr of beta^2/r^2. I_gravity enters only as the fixed constant zeta(3)/4. None of the three hypotheses of eq. 77 (b^2≈0, m≈0, mu r→0) is encoded anywhere. Negating all three changes no check, so every check passes when its hypotheses are false; that is the vacuity guard failing. The script's own check "|c|<=6.37e-64 holds as an upper bound over beta<=1 AT r=38.6 um (if |I(b^2)|<=zeta(3)/4)" rests on a premise that is false (point 4).

3. SOURCE NOW READ. The audit's grounds for OPEN no longer hold. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries and get_paper_content both returned arXiv:2309.05759v2 in full this time. Five things read at source:
- Eq. 76 (p.20) matches the restatement exactly: c^{mu nu} = -(1/16pi^2)(1/(pi r M4)^2)(b b - eta b^2/4) I_gravity.
- The paper prints the I_gravity integral: (1/(6√pi)) Σ_{w≥1} ∫∫ (9s^2-2st-11t^2+5sb^2)/(w^3 t^{1/2}(s+t)^6) exp(-s(pi m r w)^2 - t(pi mu r w)^2 - (s+t(1-b^2))/(t(s+t))).
- Eq. 77 is stated explicitly as "b^2≈0, m≈0: I_gravity ≈ -zeta(3)/4 as mu r→0".
- mu is "an infrared regulator" (p.18). It is not the electron mass, so the audit's "if mu = m_e" drift item is resolved. The fermion mass is m.
- The domain is b^2 = beta^2 ∈ (0,1), open (eq. 12). Eqs. 72-73, eq. 84 and the ~1e-21 bound citing Dreissen [14] all match the restatement.

4. FINITE CHECK, which the audit said was impossible. Scripts: verify/rederive/igrav.py and igrav_m.py, using scipy dblquad on the printed integrand.
- (a) Eq. 77 reproduces. At b^2=0, m=mu=0, I = -0.3005142258 against -zeta(3)/4 = -0.3005142258, a ratio of 1.00000000. As published, within its hypotheses, eq. 77 STANDS.
- (b) |I| is not ≤ zeta(3)/4 for b^2>0. The ratio |I|/(zeta3/4) is 1.71 at b^2=0.25, 3.55 at 0.5, 11.9 at 0.75, 54 at 0.9, 1953 at 0.99, 6.3e4 at 0.999 and 2.0e6 at 0.9999. Analytically, the region s≲t^2, t→0 gives I → -(zeta(3)/2)(1-b^2)^{-3/2} = -(zeta(3)/2)γ^3. The numerics match this to 0.9996 at 1-b^2 = 1e-4. So the audit's drift item ("the effect is an O(1) factor") is wrong. At beta=1 (b^2=1), which the tree uses at branelink.py:97 and :288-292, the printed integrand diverges. That point is also outside the paper's open domain. The tree's "beta = 1 gives |c| <= 6.37e-64" is therefore not supported even at fixed r. At m=0, the 1e-21 bound is reached at r=38.6 um once 2β²γ³ ≈ 1.57e42, i.e. γ ≈ 9.2e13.
- (c) The m≈0 hypothesis fails for the electron: pi m_e r = 3.14e8 at 38.6 um (computed). At b^2=0, I falls with m: I/(-zeta3/4) is 0.864 at pi m r = 1, 0.100 at 10 and 1.18e-3 at 100. At small b^2 this only deepens the null.

5. SOURCE-INTERNAL DISCREPANCY, recorded and not repaired. The Fig. 7 caption says I_gravity "decreases rapidly but has a finite limit as b^2→1". The printed integrand diverges as γ^3. One of the two is a misprint, or the figure plots something other than the printed integrand. Under M's rules this is a discrepancy, not a refutation of eq. 77. Either way |I(b^2→1)| > zeta(3)/4, because the integral is decreasing from -zeta(3)/4.

GRADE. The external eqs. 76-77 STAND within their stated hypotheses: verified numerically from the printed definition. The result as the tree uses it is NARROWED.
- The null holds on the bulk-graviton branch: beta ≤ 3.74e-8, b^2 ~ 1.4e-15, I = -zeta(3)/4 to O(b^2), 57 orders short. It holds at r = 38.6 um, not over all r ≤ 38.6 um, which is the audit's own wrong-way-inequality finding, reconfirmed.
- The beta=1 figure 6.37e-64 is outside both the b^2≈0 hypothesis and the paper's b^2<1 domain, where |I| grows without bound per the printed integrand. It also uses m≈0 where pi m_e r = 3e8.

The audit is refuted on two points. First, OPEN rested on the source being unreadable, and it is readable now. Second, its quantitative drift claim (O(1)) and its script's conditional upper-bound check both rest on |I| ≤ zeta(3)/4, which is false for every b^2>0.

audits.name: Clamped-beam (Euler-Bernoulli) fundamental: g'''' = mu^4 g, clamped ends, cos(mu) cosh(mu) = 1, INT (g'')^2 = mu_1^4 INT g^2

source.located: Classic: the clamped-clamped Euler-Bernoulli beam frequency equation cos(mu)cosh(mu) = 1 (Rayleigh, Theory of Sound, 1877). There is no arXiv copy, so the classic is NAMED-NOT-READ. The form the tree relies on is restated in C.J. Fewster, 'Lectures on quantum energy inequalities', arXiv:1208.5399v1 (2012), pp.10-11, Eqs. (3)-(4) and footnote 7. Its rigorous Sobolev backing is Fewster & Teo, gr-qc/9908073 (PRD 61, 084012, 2000), Thm 3.2, Lemma 3.1 and footnote 7.
source.via: The page text of 1208.5399 pp.10-11 and gr-qc/9908073 pp.1-4,7,12-16 was returned by alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries to the sister audits of this pass (audits/1208.5399.json, audits/1208.5399-w22-remark.json), and the quotations here come from those records. In this stage all alphaXiv calls were refused with 'assistant quota exceeded': answer_pdf_queries twice, get_paper_content once and discover_papers once. A direct arxiv.org fetch was refused by the egress proxy with a 403. Nothing was re-queried here. The restatement prints only 'C ~ 3.17'. No source read here prints the frequency equation cos mu cosh mu = 1, the root 4.7300..., sigma or the mode shape; those are established by derivation, not by reading.

audits.published_statement: 1208.5399 p.10: 'INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' ... 'The bound is known not to be optimal.' ... 'it remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R)'. p.11: 'Suppose that <T00>_w < rho for some interval t in [t0, t0+tau] of time. Then, for any g in C0^oo((t0,t0+tau)) ... <g|g''''>/<g|g> >= -16pi^2 rho ... the left-hand side can be minimized over g, to give the minimum eigenvalue of the operator d^4/dt^4 on [t0,t0+tau], with boundary conditions at each end corresponding to vanishing of the function and its first derivative. The upshot is that rho >= -C/tau^4, (4) where the numerical constant C ~ 3.17.' The classic content was not read and is derived here: the clamped eigenfunctions of d^4/dt^4 on [0,1] are g = cosh(mu t) - cos(mu t) - sigma(sinh(mu t) - sin(mu t)), with sigma = (cosh mu - cos mu)/(sinh mu - sin mu) and eigenvalue mu^4, where mu is a positive root of cos mu cosh mu = 1. The least root is mu_1 = 4.73004...
published_hypotheses: S1: the operator is d^4/dt^4 on a bounded interval (length tau, or [0,1] after scaling), in its self-adjoint clamped realisation, g = g' = 0 at both ends. Sources: 1208.5399 p.11; gr-qc/9908073 Thm 3.2, form domain W^{2,2}_0(I).

S2: the minimisation runs over g in C0^oo of the OPEN interval (p.11). The infimum is the least eigenvalue, and it is NOT attained in C0^oo, because the minimiser has g''(0) = 2 mu^2 != 0. Attaining it needs W^{2,2}_0: the p.10 remark, and gr-qc/9908073 Lemma 3.1 (C0^oo(I) is a form core).
S3: g is real-valued. Eq. (3) is written with g(t)^2, and the Parseval step uses the evenness of |ghat|^2 (2301.01698 eq. (1.4)).
S4: C is the optimal-sampler constant of an inequality that is itself 'known not to be optimal' (p.10). It is not a sharp QEI constant.
S5 (classic): the operator is the fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli one, with no shear or rotary-inertia terms. This is irrelevant here, because the tree uses the pure eigenproblem as mathematics.
hypothesis_drift: SCOPE (not a narrowing): fewsterteo.py:41-42 and :165 call C_F the constant 'at the OPTIMAL COMPACTLY SUPPORTED sampler'. Fewster's Eq. (4) minimises over C0^oo((t0,t0+tau)), and there the infimum is not attained. The optimal sampler exists only in W^{2,2}_0; check A6 gives g''(0) = 2 mu^2. So using the mode itself as the sampler (fewsterteo.py:224-230) rests on the p.10 W^{2,2} remark and F&T Thm 3.2, which audits/1208.5399-w22-remark.json grades STANDS. No number changes.

IMPLICIT: the IBP identity at fewsterteo.py:49-51 and :411-415 only gives the mode's own Rayleigh quotient, mu^4. That mu_1^4 is the MINIMUM is a spectral statement the tree takes from Fewster Eq. (4) (achievable.py:338-340) and from its hypothesis 'first positive root'. fewsterteo's selftest does not check this; this audit does (checks B1, D1-D5, G1-G3).

NAMED, not dropped: Fewster p.10 says Eq. (3) is 'known not to be optimal'. C_F is therefore the optimal-sampler constant of a bound that is not sharp. The tree claims no sharpness at fewsterteo.py:41-54.

REALITY of g: the Parseval step at fewsterteo.py:46-48 needs g to be real. The exponential form at fewsterteo.py:224-230 has complex coefficients but sums to the real mode to 4.9e-15 (check F3). The hypothesis is satisfied.

The tree's hypothesis that the 41-digit agreement is not independent (fewsterteo.py:52-54 and :167) is CONFIRMED: achievable.FEWSTER_C is exactly FEWSTER_MU1**4/(16 pi^2) (check E5). This audit adds an independent check by Fourier quadrature, with relative error 1.1e-7 (check H1).

audits.published_statement: Not read at source. The statement below is the textbook form, and it is what was re-derived here. A ray passing mass M at impact parameter b in the weak field is deflected toward the mass by alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b). Rays at impact parameter b from a source at infinity therefore cross the axis at f = b/alpha = b^2 c^2/(4GM). Because f grows with b, the lens has a focal line, not a focal point. For the Sun at b = R_sun the published focus is about 547.8 AU (Toth & Turyshev; search summary only).

audits.published_statement: 'The DSNEC of Equation (49) currently makes sense only on Minkowski spacetime or at length scales sufficiently smaller than the curvature scale.' (Kontou 2024, arXiv:2405.05963; wording from a search snippet, section number from DOCKET 64). The sentence before it reads: 'it is unclear what integrating over two null directions means unless they are both less than the radius of curvature.' This is a statement about scope, i.e. about where the literature currently stands. It is not a theorem.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Minkowski): the DSNEC is derived for free fields on Minkowski spacetime and renormalised against the Minkowski vacuum. This is corroborated by FFKP 2309.10848, READ at lines 3083-3094 and footnote 15. FFK 2111.05772 is NAMED-NOT-READ.

H2 (short-scale clause): alternatively, on a curved spacetime, the null smearing lengths delta+ and delta- must be 'sufficiently smaller than the curvature scale'. The sentence gives no number for 'sufficiently'. It says this is where the DSNEC 'makes sense', not that a curved-spacetime bound has been proven; FFKP footnote 15 calls the curved extension 'expected'.
Implicit in the DSNEC: the fields are free. For the non-minimally coupled field, FFKP's DSNEC form also requires <:phi^2:> <= phi_max^2 (FFKP eq. (79), READ).
hypothesis_drift: ELIDED WORDS (a discrepancy, not an error): qeihps.py:121-122 writes 'the DSNEC ... currently makes sense only on Minkowski spacetime or at length scales sufficiently smaller than the curvature scale'. The elided words are 'of Equation (49)', and the meaning is unchanged.

ADDED, and named in the tree: a Planck floor on the sampling length. The DSN row reads 'Minkowski, or sampling << curvature radius (>= l_P)' (qeihps.py:446), and qeihps.py:122-124 turns 'sufficiently smaller' into 'SUB-PLANCKIAN', hence REFUSED. Kontou's sentence has no l_P floor. Read on its own, its short-scale clause would formally admit sampling at l << 0.0243 l_P on HPS. The floor is the tree's own premise about the semiclassical regime; it cites 'Kontou's own doubt about the semiclassical regime of [90]' only as a CAVEAT (qeihps.py:113-117).

WEAKENED (flatness test): Kontou says 'Minkowski spacetime', but the owner tests 'kretschmann == 0' (qeihps.py:449). The selftest labels this 'CONTROL flat: Kretschmann 0 meets the DSNEC row' (qeihps.py:1039-1040). A vanishing Kretschmann scalar does not imply Minkowski: the vacuum plane wave ds^2 = -2du dv + (x^2-y^2)du^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 has Ricci = 0, R_uxux = -1 and Kretschmann = 0 (sympy check E1).

WEAKENED (scale test): 'min(radii) > 1' (qeihps.py:449) is necessary but not sufficient for a sampling length l with l_P <= l <= r_c/k to exist. For example, r_c = 7/4 l_P passes the test but leaves no l in [1, r_c/10] (z3 check E2).

Neither weakening affects the HPS verdict. At the HPS throat the Kretschmann scalar is 4/r_0^4, not zero, and both radii are below l_P, so the row FAILS under the tree's criterion and under a literal reading alike (checks B and D).

audits.published_statement: Hamilton & Lisle, gr-qc/0411060v2, Sec II.B, p.5: 'the mass M(r) = M - Q^2/(2r) interior to r ... the mass M at infinity, less the mass ... Q^2/(2r) contained in the electric field ... r_+- = M +- (M^2 - Q^2)^{1/2} (21). The inflow velocity beta hits the speed of light at the outer horizon r_+, reaches a maximum velocity between the outer and inner horizons, slows back down to the speed of light at the inner horizon r_-, and slows all the way to zero velocity at the turnaround radius r_0 = Q^2/2M (22) ... The RN solution describes the geometry of empty space surrounding a classical point charge of infinitesimal size, and as such consists of a gravitationally repulsive singularity of infinite negative mass sheathed in an electric field containing an infinite positive mass.' Faraoni & Vachon 2006.10827v2: in the RN inner region, which has negative quasilocal mass, 'gravity becomes repulsive, a massive test particle with zero initial velocity cannot overcome this repulsion', and this happens 'in any region with negative Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass'. Khuri-Weinstein 1307.5499 Thm 2, restating GHHP83: Einstein-Maxwell initial data with a strongly asymptotically flat end that satisfy the charged DEC mu_0 >= |J| + |rho| (eq 2) have m >= |Q|. McCormick 1907.07967 p.14: 'Clearly we can write down initial data with very small mass density and very large charge density, and then one should not expect this inequality to hold'; the bound needs (3.16) R(g) - 2|E|^2 >= 4|div E|.
published_hypotheses: Reissner-Nordstrom electrovac: source-free Maxwell field on r > 0, static and spherically symmetric, geometric Gaussian units (Hamilton-Lisle Sec II.B)
the ordering r_0 = Q^2/2M < r_- <= r_+ presupposes real horizons, i.e. |Q| <= M (eq 21: 'a spherical black hole of mass M and charge Q')
r = 0 is a singular centre ('repulsive singularity of infinite negative mass'); r < r_0 is exactly where the Misner-Sharp interior mass is negative
'repulsive' means negative Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass (Faraoni-Vachon): an E = 1 radial observer cannot enter; this is exactly f > 1, i.e. Phi > 0

Q <= M (GHHP via KW13 / McCormick) needs complete Einstein-Maxwell data with a strongly asymptotically flat end AND the charged DEC mu_0 >= |J| + |rho| (matter energy density dominates charge density)
positivity for a horizonless body (Hayward Prop 6) needs the DEC, an untrapped hypersurface and a REGULAR centre; 'the energy can be negative if the above assumptions do not hold'

Ordinary matter violates this (C9: 1 kg carrying 1 nC has Q/M = 11.6; the electron has 2.04e21), and so does a static Israel shell with positive rest mass and Q/M = 16.67 (C6). audits.published_statement: NOT QUOTED (source not read). The standard modern form, as re-derived here: if u'' + q(t) u = 0 on [a,b] has a non-trivial solution with u(a) = u(b) = 0, then (b - a) * INT_a^b q+(t) dt > 4, where q+ = max(q,0). The constant 4 is best possible and is never attained. Lyapunov's own 1892 statement is commonly reported for continuous q (often q >= 0). The sign-indefinite q+ form and the refinement INT (t-a)(b-t) q+ > b - a are commonly credited to later authors (Wintner / Hartman, c. 1951). That credit is NOT verified here.
published_hypotheses: A scalar, linear, second-order ODE u'' + q u = 0 with one unknown function. This is the standard form; it was not read at source.

q is real-valued. The classical statement (as commonly reported) takes q continuous; the modern statement takes q in L^1, with Caratheodory solutions (u in C^1, u' absolutely continuous). The L^1, sign-indefinite case is re-derived here.
u is non-trivial with two zeros a < b. They need not be consecutive: the claim reduces to consecutive zeros inside [a,b], because shrinking the interval only lowers (b-a) INT q+.
The conclusion is strict (>), and the constant 4 is sharp but never attained. Re-derived here: a centred-slab family gives 5.92, 4.61, 4.17, 4.054, 4.0053, 4.00005, falling toward 4 from above.

audits.published_statement: Theorem 5.1 (v2 p.14), verbatim apart from extraction artefacts: 'Consider an Einstein static universe of radius a > 0, a cosmological constant Lambda in R and a free scalar quantum field of mass m >= 0 and scalar curvature coupling xi in R such that c := m^2 a^2 + 6 xi - 1 > -1. Fix renormalisation constants alpha_1..alpha_5, beta_1..beta_3 in R and define Y_1 (93), Y_2 (94) ... in terms of R = 6/a^2 and the numbers defined in (131), (133), (86), (87) and (90). Then the set S_qf of symmetric quasi-free states omega that solve the semi-classical Einstein equation (1) is in bijective correspondence with sequences {a_n}_{n>=0} subset R_{>=0} such that m^2 sum a_n = Y_1 (95), sum a_n l_n^2/a^2 = Y_2 (96), where the correspondence is given by Theorem 3.1.' Corollary 5.2 covers S, the set of all solutions with a symmetric two-point distribution, quasi-free or not: (1) S contains the ground state iff Y_1 = Y_2 = 0; (2) for m = 0, S is nonempty iff Y_2 >= Y_1 = 0; (3) for m > 0, S is nonempty iff Y_1 = Y_2 = 0 or m^2 Y_2 >= (m^2 + xi R) Y_1 > 0; (4) more than one solution implies infinitely many; (5) S is a singleton iff it contains the ground state. Intro: 'ultra-static spacetimes with maximally symmetric spatial slices ... spatially compact ... In particular, we require the spacetime to be given by Einstein's static universe M = R x S^3, g = -dt^2 + a^2 h'. Sec. 7: the renormalisation parameters 'cannot be determined without further input, either from observations or from an underlying theory of quantum gravity'.
published_hypotheses: H1 spacetime: exactly the Einstein static universe R x S^3 with a round S^3 of radius a > 0 (eq. 2). It is ultrastatic and spatially compact. No quotient S^3/Gamma is treated, and the open case is left as future work.
H2 matter: a single free real scalar quantum field of mass m >= 0 and coupling xi in R.
H3 c := m^2 a^2 + 6 xi - 1 > -1, which is equivalent to m^2 + xi R > 0 (a ground state exists).

H4 states: the two-point distribution respects all the symmetries of the metric, R x SO(4). Theorem 5.1 also requires the state to be quasi-free; Corollary 5.2 drops that requirement. Hadamard is not assumed.
H5 renormalisation: the constants alpha_1..alpha_5 and beta_1..beta_3 are fixed but arbitrary, and the symmetry reduces the freedom to the perfect-fluid form (89).
H6 equation: the full fourth-order semiclassical Einstein equation. The paper only argues, and does not prove, that the reduced-order formulation gives the same conclusions.

H7 existence is conditional: whether S is empty, a singleton or infinite depends on (a, Lambda, m, xi) and on the renormalisation constants through Y_1 and Y_2. For example, m = 0 with kappa' > 0 and Lambda' < R/4 gives no solutions.

audits.published_statement: FLAG 2024 (2411.04268v3 p.260): 'The matrix elements of the scalar operator qq with flavour q give the rate of change in the nucleon mass due to nonzero values of the corresponding quark mass. This relationship is given by the Feynman-Hellmann theorem ... sigma_piN = m_ud <N|uu + dd|N> (431), sigma_s = m_s <N|ss|N> (432), sigma_c = m_c <N|cc|N> (433)'. p.261: 'The sigma_piN,s,c give the shift in M_N due to nonzero light-, strange- and charm-quark masses'. Eq.(446): sigma_piN = m_ud dM_N/dm_ud. Coc et al. 2007 (astro-ph/0610733v2 p.4): strange gives '~0.19 Delta m_s/m_s' and u, d give '~0.052 Delta m_q/m_q. This implies that Delta m_p/m_p ~ 0.76 Delta Lambda/Lambda + 0.24 (Delta h/h + Delta v/v) (11)'. Eq.(13): 'Lambda = mu (m_c m_b m_t/mu^3)^(2/27) exp(-2 pi/(9 alpha_s(mu))) for mu > m_t'. Eq.(14): Delta Lambda/Lambda = R Delta alpha/alpha + (2/27)(3 Delta v/v + Delta h_c/h_c + Delta h_b/h_b + Delta h_t/h_t). Hoferichter et al. 2015, eq.(24): 'sum_{q=u,...,t} f_q^N = 2/9 + 7/9 (f_u^N + f_d^N + f_s^N) = 0.305 +- 0.009'. Flambaum 2007 p.4: 'The proton mass is proportional to Lambda_QCD (M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD)'. Hill-Solon eq.(39): the heavy-quark matrix element is a series in alpha_s/pi whose O(alpha_s^0) term is (1/(3 beta_0))(2 - 2 lambda), where lambda is the sum of the light-quark scalar matrix elements. Hill-Solon p.15: 'poorly convergent alpha_s(m_c) expansion'.
published_hypotheses: FH-1: an isolated, non-degenerate eigenvalue of a Hermitian H(lambda) with a normalised eigenstate. The nucleon is the lowest state in its channel, so this holds (machine-checked here, check B).
FH-2 (FLAG eq.(446)): sigma_q is a first-order derivative at the physical point, m_q dM_N/dm_q, of renormalized operators. m_q qq is RG invariant, so sigma_q does not depend on the scheme.
HOM-1 (Coc eqs.(11)-(12)): QCD only. m_p depends on Lambda and the quark masses alone, and the mass dimension is repaired with powers of Lambda. QED and weak contributions to m_p are left out.

HOM-2 (implicit in any homogeneity statement; derived in check C): the quark masses held fixed while Lambda varies are RG-invariant masses. If m_q(mu0) is held fixed at a scale mu0 fixed in GeV, the coefficient becomes 1 - S(1 + gamma_m(mu0)).
HOM-3 (Coc eq.(11), Hoferichter eq.(24), Hill-Solon lambda): the light set is u, d, s, the flavours of the theory whose scale is Lambda_3. So S = (sigma_piN + sigma_s)/m_N.

H1-1 (Coc eqs.(13)-(14), Hoferichter eq.(24), SVZ via Hill-Solon eq.(39)): one-loop running with continuous leading-order matching at each heavy threshold; c, b and t treated in the heavy-quark limit; Standard Model coloured content between m_t and the high scale (Coc footnote 1).
H1-2 (Coc eq.(14)): m_Q = h_Q v at fixed Yukawa. The tree's H1 is Coc's case Delta alpha = 0, Delta h = 0.
H2 (Flambaum p.4): Lambda_QCD fixed and M_p proportional to it. Flambaum sets S -> 0; the tree keeps S.

audits.lacked_data: The identities themselves (Feynman-Hellmann, homogeneity, the full-theory Euler relation) lack no data: they are exact and no datum can move them (checks A, B, D). What the published numerical forms lacked: Coc et al. 2007 had no lattice sigma_s and used B_s = 1.5, giving S = 0.24. Today S_uds is 0.093-0.111, so their 0.76 becomes 0.89-0.91. That datum moved by a factor of 2.2-2.6, which supports M's hypothesis in its weak form. SVZ and the one-loop 2/9 lacked the O(alpha_s^1..3) decoupling coefficients and the Hill-Solon series; with them the H1 value rises 4.8% at S = 0.06. Evidence either way on the conclusion, computed with address.py's own functions: no quantity that rests on this result changes sign, and each moves by less than 5% (6.8% at the valence row). K_mu < 0 holds exactly for S < 1 at leading order, and beyond it whenever sum f_q < 1 (currently about 0.32-0.33). So the new data narrow the exactness of the H1 formula and move the published S, but refute nothing. The strong form of M's hypothesis is not supported for this result.
audits.grade_evidence: The core step is exact under its hypotheses and machine-checked (sympy A and B): Feynman-Hellmann plus homogeneity gives d ln m_p/d ln Lambda = 1 - S. It matches FLAG eqs.(431)-(433) and (446) and Coc 2007 eq.(11), both read at source. The tree's H1 and H2 forms, all its printed numbers and its own functions are reproduced (check D). The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree does not name three hypotheses. (1) 2/9 + 7S/9 is the leading-order evaluation of the exact sum_{u..t} f_q; beyond leading order f(0.06) is 0.28177, not 0.26889 (address.py:99-104 and 816-822 carry no LO qualifier). (2) The result is QCD only: the electromagnetic part of m_p is dropped at address.py:100. (3) Which quark mass is held fixed is unstated (check C), though the tree's use satisfies it. It is not WRONG: no counterexample exists. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT: the moved or contested inputs change numbers only. K_mu < 0 holds exactly for S < 1, |K_H2/K_H1| = 9/7, and no quantity resting on the result flips sign or moves more than 7%. Recorded as discrepancies, not repaired: '0.229' is a truncation, and S_MID omits sigma_s (see sibling sigma-term-scan).
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree states the leading-order qualifier on 2/9 + 7S/9 (or carries the full sum_{u..t} f_q) and names the QCD-only and RG-invariant-mass hypotheses. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a conclusion that turned on S or on the beyond-LO shift; none does. To WRONG: a sum_{u..t} f_q >= 1 (which would flip the sign of K_mu), or a degenerate nucleon level that breaks Feynman-Hellmann; no source read shows either. OPEN does not apply, because every step is closed-form and checked here.

audits.published_statement: BFKLW 1509.02542 p.2 (as READ in the sibling audit): 'the right hand side can have any sign ... By integrating the QNEC along a null generator, we can obtain the ANEC, in situations where the boundary term S'_out vanishes at early and late times.' The QNEC, eq (2.2): <T_kk(p)> >= hbar/(2 pi sqrt(h(p))) delta^2 S_out/delta lambda(p)^2. This is the diagonal (delta-function) coefficient of the second functional derivative, at a point on a stationary null surface where the expansion and shear vanish. BFKW 1706.09432 eq (1.3) gives the integrated per-generator form: Q_-(A,B;y) = INT_{dA}^{dB} dx^- <T_--> - (1/2pi) dS(B)/dx^-(y) + (1/2pi) dS(A)/dx^-(y) >= 0, in flat space with locally stationary cuts.
published_hypotheses: H1: the boundary term S'_out vanishes at early AND late times. BFKLW state this as a CONDITION ('in situations where'), not as a consequence.
H2: the generator belongs to a stationary null surface of a FIXED background with no dynamical gravity (BFKLW p.4). BFKW work in flat space only; CF use Minkowski Rindler cuts.
H3: <T_kk> is the renormalised expectation value in a quantum STATE of a QFT in the proved class, and S_out is that state's entanglement entropy outside the cut.

H4: S''_out is the DIAGONAL coefficient of the second functional derivative. The per-generator integral that yields [S'] is BFKW eq (1.3), with S' the local first variation at the two cuts, not the FTC of an ordinary second derivative.
H5: an affine parameter along the generator, and locally stationary cuts (vanishing expansion and shear; BFKW K^+_ij = 0).
H6: CF additionally assume the state has finite averaged null energy.

audits.lacked_data: No empirical datum enters this step. It is FTC applied to a proved inequality plus a boundary condition on the state, and hbar/2pi is exact, so no physicist 'lacked data' that would move it, and none has moved. What BFKLW (2015) lacked was a general handle on the boundary term, hence 'in situations where'. Later work filled that from the other side: FLPW and HKT (2016) proved flat-space ANEC directly, and CF (2018) showed QNEC and ANEC are equivalent for Minkowski Rindler cuts. Later literature therefore CONFIRMS the conclusion in its class. The evidence the other way concerns the tree's use. R2 and R3 show the boundary condition carries the whole conclusion and is not implied by the inequalities, and the tree asserts it on a curved background with a classical T and no state. The tree's own anecscope.py:24-27 concedes curved-space ANEC is false in general. R4 shows the only escape route, [S'] != 0, would need a Planck-density entropy gradient (1.3-2.0 times S_BH per bubble radius), outside every fixed-background proof. More data would not change the step. A curved-space theorem or a computed state would change the tree's use.

audits.published_statement: HPS p.3: 'we employ the stress-energy tensor of Anderson, Hiscock and Samuel, which is calculated for a quantized scalar field in an arbitrary static and spherically symmetric spacetime [18].' p.4: 'An accurate analytic approximation to the exact numerically calculated scalar field stress energy tensor was developed in Ref. [18]', then eq. (4) and, 'for a conformally coupled scalar (xi = 1/6) ... (K^2 = 1/5760 pi)', eqs. (5)-(7). Fn [20]: 'm = kappa = 0. In this case, the arbitrary renormalization scale parameter mu ... can be absorbed into the definition of f.' Eq. (8) is the quartic for r(0). With f(0)=f''(0)=1 and r''(0)=0 it gives 'r(0) ~ 67 l_P'. Eq. (9) data: -1 <= ln f(0) < 0, r(0) = sqrt(-16K^2 ln f(0)), and the throat is '~0.02 l_P' at ln f(0) = -2/3. p.8: 'omega_1^2 = 1/(16K^2) and omega_2^2 = 1/(16K^2(4+3 ln F)) ... F(l) ~ (a ln l - b)^2, a = 5.3, b = 25.5 ... the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat ... local solutions which correspond to large throat (r(0) ~ 200 - 300 l_P) wormholes with horizons located far from the throat ... A full account ... will appear in a separate publication.' Popov p.1: AHS's expressions were 'obtained ... in static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat spacetimes'. Popov p.2: the high-frequency part 'does not depend on the quantum state'; the low-frequency part is 'calculated in asymptotically flat spacetime' (eq. 70). Popov p.10: his (T)^(4) is 'equivalent to the analytical approximations ... of Anderson, Hiscock, and Samuel'. Popov Sec. VI: validity conditions (83), lambda << sqrt(f)/w_0 << L. The restatements of AHS's scope DISAGREE: HPS says 'arbitrary static spherically symmetric', and Arrechea App. B says 'purely geometrical and invoke no additional assumptions about the spacetime', while Popov p.1 says 'asymptotically flat'. On accuracy: AHL shows that on extreme RN the approximation predicts a horizon divergence the exact numerics lack. Arrechea p.3 says it is good in Schwarzschild, worse in RN, and that its accuracy elsewhere 'is yet to be known'.
published_hypotheses: AHS, via restatements: a scalar field of mass m and arbitrary coupling xi on a static spherically symmetric spacetime, in the zero-temperature vacuum with respect to the timelike Killing vector or in a thermal state. Whether asymptotic flatness is a hypothesis of the DERIVATION is CONTESTED between restatements: Popov p.1 says yes; HPS p.3 and Arrechea p.2 / App. B say no. AHS's own text was NOT READ.

The AHS analytic part is the 4th-order WKB high-frequency part. Its cutoff lambda (= w_0) and scale mu (= m_DS) are arbitrary and must be 'fixed by experiment'. It is conserved and carries the trace anomaly for the conformal field.

Using <T>_analytic alone as <T>_ren drops <T>_num, which has to be checked background by background (Arrechea p.3). Popov's own conditions are (70), asymptotic flatness for the low-frequency part, and (83).
HPS: G = 8 pi <T>_analytic; xi = 1/6; m = kappa = 0; mu absorbed into the normalization of f; ds^2 = -f dt^2 + dl^2 + r^2 dOmega^2; G = hbar = c = 1.
HPS throat data: r(0) > 0, r'(0) = f'(0) = 0, f(0) > 0, symmetric data, eq. (9) with -1 <= ln f(0) < 0. The ll equation is a constraint.
HPS method: numerical integration plus an asymptotic analysis 'guided by the numerical investigation'. The 200-300 l_P solutions are 'local', have horizons, and are not shown.

later_literature.what: Splits <T>_ren into a high-frequency part, which is the AHS analytic part, state-independent and derived without asymptotic flatness, and a low-frequency part computed only for asymptotically flat spacetimes (eq. 70). Gives the validity conditions (83). This is the tree's domain witness, published 6 years after HPS.
The AHS analytic approximation predicts a horizon divergence on extreme RN that the exact numerics lack. It can fail qualitatively even on an asymptotically flat background.

Restates AHS as carrying 'no additional assumptions about the spacetime', which contradicts Popov p.1. Says its adequacy is unknown away from black holes. App. B: the AHS <T> diverges like 1/r at a regular centre unless the odd Taylor coefficients vanish. Fourth-order non-perturbative branches are non-physical under Simon's criterion, and HPS is cited as the example. The authors nevertheless solve the equations self-consistently themselves, so the point is contested rather than settled.

Computes the exact Hadamard <T> (Levi-Ori mode sum) on an asymptotically flat zero-tidal wormhole, and states that before it, exact wormhole <T> existed only in the short-throat flat-space model. No exact <T> exists on HPS-type metrics. The paper does not test AHS.
Restates AHS as a general method on static spherically symmetric black-hole backgrounds. Used here only as a restatement of AHS's scope.

audits.lacked_data: What HPS had in 1997: AHS validated in Schwarzschild and RN, and AHL 1995 already showing the approximation failing at the extreme-RN horizon. What came later: (a) Popov 2003: using the analytic part as the full <T> is justified only with a low-frequency part computed for asymptotically flat spacetimes, and HPS's metric is not asymptotically flat (their own p.8). (b) The order-reduction view, applied explicitly to AHS and to HPS by Arrechea 2023. Computed here: HPS's ripple wavenumber 1/(4K) goes as hbar^(-1/2), with wavelength 0.187 l_P. (c) Arrechea's regular-centre caveat. (d) Exact mode-sum methods, which have not yet been run on any HPS-type metric. Does it change the conclusion? For HPS's model-system claim: no. The system re-derives, and the two misprints are decided by conservation; a misprint is a discrepancy, not a refutation. For 'a solution of semiclassical gravity / evidence for wormholes': the later work moves this from untested to doubtful on two counts, but no exact <T>_ren on an HPS metric exists, so it is OPEN in the literature, not refuted. For the tree: m < 0 is already confined to HPS's model system and to outside the established domain, so the later data reinforce O5 OPEN and add one more named limitation. Evidence against M's hypothesis here: the external mathematics checks, with an anomaly coefficient matching AHL. What was missing was domain information, not correct mathematics.
audits.grade_evidence: (1) HPS's system, its conserved reading (unique among four readings), eq. (8), the radii 0.02428 and 67.26 l_P, omega_1 and omega_2, and the anomaly trace were all RE-DERIVED in sympy from a fresh transcription and agree (26/26). This independently confirms the tree's M1/M2 conservation logic. (2) The domain hypothesis is quoted accurately from Popov. Its 'derived' half is contested by HPS p.3 and Arrechea App. B; its 'established' half is supported. AHS itself is NAMED-NOT-READ, so the domain claim rests on restatement only. (3) R7, O5 and hpscentre drop the non-perturbative-in-hbar limitation (k ~ hbar^(-1/2), computed here) that the later literature attaches to exactly these solutions, naming HPS. (4) The 300 l_P figure drops 'local, not shown'. Nothing is contradicted or computed false, and no moved datum moves anything: l_P is unchanged and mu has never been measured. The tree's conclusion (m < 0 in HPS's system, not inside the established domain, O5 OPEN) is unchanged and is narrowed further in its own direction. The grade is not STANDS because a limitation is unnamed and the source is read only through disagreeing restatements. It is not WRONG because no contradiction was shown. It is not OPEN because the load-bearing mathematics was checkable and was checked.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: R7, O5 and hpscentre name the order-reduction (non-perturbative in hbar) limitation and the contested scope of AHS; throatmass labels 300 l_P 'local, not shown'; and AHS PRD 51 4337 is read at source. Toward WRONG for the tree's use: an exact <T>_ren (for example a Levi-Ori mode sum) on HPS's metric showing that the AHS analytic part is accurate there and that m < 0 survives. An AHS reading at source showing that asymptotic flatness is a hypothesis of the derivation would retire drift item 1. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a measurement of mu, which does not exist.

audits.published_statement: (a) INSTANTON, RS96 eqs.(2.7)-(2.8) (alphaXiv p.7): 'The instanton action is S_inst = 8 pi^2/g^2 and the tunnelling amplitude is proportional to A_inst ~ e^{-S_inst}. In the electroweak theory, the tunneling probability is unobservably small, Gamma_inst ~ exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) ~ 10^-170, where alpha_W = g^2/4pi = alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29.' Tye-Wong 1505.03690 printed p.7: 'since an instanton action S = 2 pi/alpha_W where the weak coupling alpha_W ~ 1/29.7, the tunneling rate goes like exp(-2S) ~ 10^-162, which is totally unobservable.' (b) SPHALERON, TW eq.(1.2) printed p.3: 'Using the known Higgs vacuum expectation value v = 246 GeV, W Boson mass m_W = 80 GeV and the Higgs Boson mass m_H = 125 GeV, we obtain V(Q) ~ 4.75 TeV (1.31 sin^2(m_W Q) + 0.60 sin^4(m_W Q)), E_sph = max[V(Q)] = V(pi/2m_W) = 9.11 TeV'; printed p.4: 'turning on the U(1) coupling (i.e., Weinberg angle sin^2 theta_W = 0.23) will lower the sphaleron energy by about a percent. So it is reasonable to use E_sph = 9.0 TeV'. FFS eq.(10): 'E_sph = g_2 v V(pi/2) ~ 9.08 TeV', with beta_1 = 1.313, beta_2 = 0.603 (eq.(8)). (c) COLLIDER RATE. BLRRT hep-ph/0304180 abstract: 'baryon and lepton number violation remains exponentially suppressed up to very high energies of at least 30 sphaleron masses (250 TeV)'; p.2: 'This approach is based on the conjecture that, with exponential accuracy, the two-particle initial state can be substituted by a multiparticle one ... (although not proven rigorously ...)'. Khoze-Milne 2011.07167 printed p.9: 'Electroweak instantons remain exponentially suppressed by at least e^{-(4pi/alpha_w) 0.70} and are unobservable in high energy 2 particle collisions for any value of the energy'; p.13: 'while there is no rigorous proof of exponentiation'; p.15: 'based in part on an assumption that there are no additional exponentially growing ... contributions'. FFS p.4: 'in the leading order of the WKB approximation ... a suppression factor ~ e^{-pi E_sph/m_W} ~ 10^-155 ... (1/(4pi)^2)^80 ~ 10^-176 ... Those types of the suppressions still remain regardless of the band structure'. Tye-Wong 1505.03690 abstract: 'baryon-lepton number violating processes can take place without the exponential tunneling suppression (at zero temperature) at energies around and above the barrier height (sphaleron energy) at 9.0 TeV'. 1710.07223 p.1: 'there is a discrepancy of about 70 orders of magnitude between the two estimates'; p.2: 'We agree with this estimate for a single sphaleron. However, we claim that multi-sphaleron processes can drastically change the picture ... both estimates involve assumptions based on intuitions as well as approximations remaining to be fully justified'; p.3: 'the estimate (4) is only an order of magnitude guesstimate'. CMS 1805.06013: 'An upper limit of 0.021 is set at 95% confidence level on the fraction of all quark-quark interactions above the nominal threshold energy of 9 TeV resulting in the sphaleron transition.'
published_hypotheses: 't Hooft / RS96 / KM (instanton factor): the leading semiclassical (weak-coupling) exponent of the zero-energy, zero-temperature rate, exp(-2 S_inst) = exp(-4pi/alpha_W) with S_inst = 8pi^2/g^2; constrained instantons in the Higgs phase; no prefactor; the coupling's scheme and scale are not fixed at this order (RS96 uses alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29; TW uses 1/29.7 and ~1/30; Matchev-Verner use alpha_W ~ 0.034).
TW15 / E_sph: theta_W = 0, right-handed fermions ignored (printed p.5); classical static saddle on Manton's path; inputs v = 246, m_W = 80, m_H = 125 GeV; zero temperature.

TW15 / collider claim: the field theory reduced to 1-D quantum mechanics in the Chern-Simons coordinate with constant mass m = 17.1 TeV; Bloch waves of the periodic potential; zero temperature; the 10^{4+-2} event count is 'A very crude order of magnitude estimate', with F_EW and kappa taken 'for lack of better information'.

FFS / E_sph and rebuttal: U(1)_Y neglected ('a few %', p.1); gauge-invariant reduced model with A_0; WKB with three connection formulas; the 10^-155 rests on the coherent-state formalism of their Refs.[12,13], 'in the leading order of the WKB approximation'; two-particle in-state; no thermal corrections.

BLRRT / prevalent result: SU(2)-Higgs model 'with theta_W = 0' (p.3); 'lambda = 0.125, which corresponds to M_H = M_W', with 'The dependence on the Higgs boson mass is very weak' asserted (p.3); spherical symmetry, so the results hold 'strictly speaking, to s-wave scattering only' (p.2); the few-particle conjecture 'although not proven rigorously' (p.2); smooth N -> 0 extrapolation.

Khoze-Milne: optical-theorem instanton / anti-instanton calculation with initial-state (Mueller) corrections; exponentiation assumed ('no rigorous proof', p.13); no additional exponentially growing higher-order terms assumed (pp.13, 15); pre-exponential factors not computed (p.16).
TW17: multi-sphaleron resonant tunnelling; d ~ 4 effective (B+L)-conserving dimensions; a power-law (not exponential) prefactor assumed.
